articles.title: World Darts Championship: Schedule, format, previous winners and nine darters at Alexandra Palace
articles.summary: There is less than a month to go before London's amphitheatre of arrows, Alexandra Palace, kickstarts the festive period by hosting the World Darts Championships 2027; watch all the action on Sky Sports from Friday December 11th
articles.body:
A total of 128 players will arrive ready to let fly, but only one will leave crowned as world champion and claim the joint largest prize in the sport's history... £1m.

Alongside this record prize pot, the event will for the first time be held in the Alexandra Palace's Great Hall, meaning new attendance records will be set.

When is the 2027 World Darts Championship?

The 34th World Darts Championship starts on Friday December 11, running until Thursday January 3, 2027.

Arrows will be flying every day over the festive period, except for Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, Boxing Day, and New Year's Eve.

Where is the 2027 World Darts Championship?

Alexandra Palace's West Hall has been the competition's home for over 19 years.

However, this year fans will revel in all the action in the Great Hall, which has allowed for the sale of around 180,000 tickets across all sessions.

More fans, a bigger atmosphere, but at the same legendary venue.

Who has already qualified for 2027 World Darts Championships?

Forty-eight of the 128 players competing have earned their places via international and association qualifying events wth the remaining 80 places going to those top-ranked on the PDC Order of Merit (40) and ProTour Order of Merit (40) circuits.

Thirty-eight players have already earned their place at the oche via these qualifiers; most recently Gary Mawson, José Marquês and Anton Östlund via the CDC Continental Cup, PDCE Mediterranean Qualifier and PDC Nordic & Baltic Championship respectively.

Though not officially secured, reigning champion Luke Littler, former World No 1 Luke Humphries and darting royalty Michael van Gerwen are mathematically assured to be there.

Ten places at the oche remain, though that does include the World Youth Championship Final on November 29. If the winner has already qualified via the ProTour, then that place will defer to the Tour Card Holder Qualifier.

November 13: PDC Europe Super League (DACH) - 1 place

November 13: PDO Polish Qualifier - 1 place

November 14: Netherlands & Belgium Qualifier - 1 place

November 28: South-East Europe Qualifier - 1 place

November 29: Czech Republic Qualifier - 1 place

November 30: PDC Tour Card Holder Qualifier - 4+ places

Nineteen-year-old sensation, Luke 'The Nuke' Littler enters this year's tournament as the two-time reigning champion.

Last year, Littler defeated Gian van Veen 7-1 to retain the Sid Waddell Trophy and become the fourth player in PDC history to win consecutive World Championships, following Phil Taylor, Adrian Lewis and Gary Anderson.

Littler is the current world number one and already has 30 senior PDC titles, including 14 major singles, ranking him third on the all-time PDC major winners list.

In 1994, the total prize fund was £64,000. Today, each of the 128 players competing is guaranteed at least £15,000 each just for making the first round and a total prize fund of £5m will be played for

Last year, the prize for first place doubled from £500,000 to a record-shattering £1m - which remains the same this year.

This makes it the joint-highest winner's prize pot in the sport's history.

The runner-up will receive £400,000 and the two losing semi-finalists £200,000 each.

Watch the World Darts Championship (December 11-January 3) all live on Sky Sports. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

articles.title: UTEP Fires Scotty Walden: Miners Move On From Head Coach After Wyoming Loss
articles.summary: UTEP has fired third-year coach Scotty Walden with the Miners on an eight-game losing streak.
articles.body: UTEP has fired third-year coach Scotty Walden with the Miners on an eight-game losing streak. The school announced the move Monday, a day after Walden's 37th birthday. UTEP lost 27-15 to Wyoming in its home finale on Saturday. Walden finished 6-28 with the Miners, who are 1-9 this season in their Mountain West Conference debut. They were 2-10 last year after going 3-9 in his debut with them. "His tenure has been marked by unprecedented success in recruiting and record-breaking team academic performance. He has excelled at community relations and fundraising, and has put his own money back into the program," athletic director Jim Senter said. "We haven’t seen the necessary improvement from year one to year three and believe it’s time for new leadership." The Miners have only one winning season in the past 12 years, a 7-6 record in 2021. They have to win their final two games this season to avoid losing at least 10 games for the 22nd time since 1973. UTEP didn't immediately name an interim head coach for the rest of this season. The final two games are on the road, against Air Force on Friday and at Northern Illinois on Nov. 28. After a 51-0 loss at then-No. 10 Oklahoma to open this year, the Miners beat FCS team Texas Southern 51-10. They haven't won since and scored only 91 points in their eight-game losing streak, with their most points in that stretch coming in a 52-17 loss at then-No. 19 Michigan. Walden arrived at UTEP from Austin Peay, where he was 26-14 in a tenure that started with the spring season in early 2021 after the COVID-19 pandemic shortened the 2020 season. The Governors were 9-3 in his final season and made the FCS playoffs. He had replaced Dana Dimel, who had five losing seasons in his six years with the Miners. Walden was the interim replacement for Jay Hopson at Southern Miss one game into that pandemic-altered 2020 season. He resigned after four games to take the Austin Peay job and prepare for the unusual spring season. His head coaching career started in 2016 at Division III East Texas Baptist, where he was the offensive coordinator for three years before getting promoted. Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Klopp's Germany Routs Xavi's Netherlands To Book Nations League Quarterfinals
articles.summary: Florian Wirtz has scored twice and Germany has booked its place in the Nations League quarterfinals.
articles.body: Florian Wirtz scored twice and Germany booked its place in the Nations League quarterfinals by routing the Netherlands 5-0 in Berlin on Monday. More importantly, it was confirmation of the German team’s renaissance under new coach Jürgen Klopp, whose appointment ushered in new optimism around his young team with progress evident over his six games in charge. Nico Schlotterbeck was the oldest goalscorer at 26, Wirtz is still just 23, the 24-year-old Derry Scherhant broke the deadlock, and Brajan Gruda, 22, set up two goals and scored one on what was just his second appearance for Germany. He also scored on his debut in Friday’s 3-1 win in Serbia. It was the most emphatic win for Germany under Klopp, and the worst loss so far for Netherlands manager Xavi Hernandez. The World Cup-winning Spanish midfielder and club legend at Barcelona took over the Dutch job in August. Klopp clearly enjoyed each of the goals, but he praised the players' work rate as key. "Everyone who was here today is going home with a smile, and won’t be questioning the German national team for the next three or four months. That’s a good thing," Klopp said, referring to the previous negativity around the side. "When you think of the German team, this could develop into something, and that’s good." Substitute Giorgos Masouras’ 69th-minute strike was enough for Greece to beat Serbia 1-0 at home in the other group game, but it was not enough for progress as Germany and the Netherlands both look forward to Friday's quarterfinal draw. All three teams finished with 11 points. Germany Flying Local favorite Scherhant twice hit the post before opening the scoring with a brilliant strike before the break, cutting inside to elude Dutch captain Denzel Dumfries and then shooting inside the top right corner. Bart Verbruggen got his fingers to the ball but couldn’t prevent its progress. Scherhant, who used to score such goals in the same stadium for Hertha Berlin, pointed to the ground to indicate he was home again. "You couldn't have imagined it going any better," said Scherhant, who now plays for Freiburg. Wirtz's goal, on the hour mark, was arguably better, winning the ball back from Dumfries after an attack broke down, feigning with his right foot to set up his left and then unleashing the ball in off the left post from outside the penalty area. Schlotterbeck sealed the result five minutes later with a low header to Gruda’s free kick, and Wirtz volleyed in his second in the 71st after Gruda was left free on the right. It prompted some Dutch fans to head for the exits. Gruda got Germany’s fifth in the 77th, prompting furious Dutch goalkeeper Verbruggen to call a team meeting to remonstrate with his teammates. By then it was too late. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: ‘A long journey’: Ottawa Senators’ Tyler Boucher finally gets his NHL debut after battling years of setbacks
articles.summary: Tyler Boucher, drafted 10th overall by the Ottawa Senators in 2021, finally debuts in the NHL after years of injuries and setbacks, showcasing perseverance and determination to reach his dream.
articles.body: Tyler Boucher is finally getting the opportunity he has chased since the Ottawa Senators selected him 10th overall in the 2021 NHL Draft. After four surgeries and several injury-plagued seasons, the 23-year-old forward has been recalled from the Belleville Senators ahead of his NHL debut against the Winnipeg Jets.The milestone is all the more meaningful for Boucher’s family, including his father, former NHL goaltender Brian Boucher. This is a story of perseverance, rehabilitation, and determination through years of injuries to reach his dream of playing in the NHL.Tyler Boucher finally earns Ottawa Senators NHL opportunityTyler Boucher is set to make his long-awaited NHL debut with the Ottawa Senators after years of battling injuries and setbacks. His opportunity comes following winger Hayden Hodgson's groin injury during Ottawa's 4-1 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins.Boucher was called up from the Belleville Senators, Ottawa’s American Hockey League affiliate, to fill the roster spot and is expected to join Stephen Halliday and Sammy Blais on the fourth line against the Winnipeg Jets.The call-up is huge for the forward who has waited more than five years since being picked 10th overall in the 2021 NHL Draft.Why has Tyler Boucher faced so many setbacks?Boucher’s career has been marred by injuries, including four surgeries that stalled his development and minutes.Drafted in 2021, he’s played two injury-plagued seasons with the Ontario Hockey League’s Ottawa 67’s. He also faced challenges with his transition to the American Hockey League, as staying healthy was a recurring obstacle.Boucher, however, kept chasing his NHL dream. He has shown promising signs this season with Belleville.Before the call-up, he had five goals and 10 points in 17 games. He also scored in Belleville's 3-1 win over Cleveland on Sunday, giving the organization another reason to think about him for the opening.His father, Brian, said he was proud of his son's determination and his ability to overcome difficult circumstances. He stressed perseverance, resilience, and the fight it takes to keep chasing an NHL career through repeated injuries. Through his recoveries, the family had been behind Tyler and invested in his ambition to represent Ottawa.It’s a good opportunity for him, Senators head coach Travis Green also said. He admitted that Boucher had previously been prevented from being called up because of injuries.Boucher kept getting better as a player in tough circumstances, Green said. He added that he hopes the NHL debut is the start of a longer tenure with the organization.For Boucher, the chance is more than a first NHL appearance. It’s the reward for years of rehab, patience, and persistence after a rocky start to his pro career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sidney Crosby's Pittsburgh Penguins future enters an uncertain phase as Kyle Dubas prepares for possible NHL roster changes
articles.summary: Explore the uncertainties surrounding Sidney Crosby's future with the Pittsburgh Penguins as GM Kyle Dubas prepares for potential roster changes amid a rocky season.
articles.body: The Pittsburgh Penguins are facing important decisions about their veteran core, with captain Sidney Crosby's future becoming a central question. General manager Kyle Dubas is reportedly willing to honor Crosby's wishes, whether he chooses to continue in Pittsburgh, retire, or request a trade.The 39-year-old center is in the final months of his deal, and the Penguins' rocky start has raised questions about the direction of the franchise. Crosby has spent his entire 22-season NHL career with Pittsburgh, making his next decision particularly significant for the organization and its supporters.Sidney Crosby's Pittsburgh Penguins future remains in his handsSidney Crosby will have the final say over his future with the Pittsburgh Penguins, according to The Athletic's Josh Yohe. General manager Kyle Dubas is reportedly prepared to accommodate the captain's wishes, even if that means arranging a trade.Yohe explained in his November 16 report that Pittsburgh would not force Crosby into a particular outcome. If the veteran center wants to continue playing for the Penguins beyond the 2026-27 season, the organization is expected to make that possible. Retirement would also be respected, while a trade request would prompt Dubas to explore a deal.Sidney Crosby's contract situation adds to Pittsburgh's uncertaintyCrosby's current contract expires after the 2026-27 NHL season. The 39-year-old signed a two-year, $17.4 million contract with an average annual value of $8.7 million in September. Through 20 games, he has recorded 13 points, according to recent reporting, while Pittsburgh has struggled to establish consistency.Despite the difficult start, Crosby continues to add to his historic NHL achievements. Earlier in November, he moved past Marcel Dionne into sixth place on the league's all-time points list.Evgeni Malkin also faces an uncertain Penguins futureCrosby is not the only Pittsburgh veteran whose future could become a major talking point. Evgeni Malkin is also approaching the end of his contract, and the 40-year-old center could face a similar decision about his next career move.According to Yohe, the Penguins are comfortable allowing Malkin to finish the 2026-27 season in Pittsburgh. Any potential trade would require his approval, meaning the defenseman would have considerable control over his next destination.Yohe believes Karlsson could consider joining a legitimate Stanley Cup contender despite his contractual protection. Such a move would potentially give the veteran another opportunity to compete for the championship that has remained missing from his NHL career.Letang's future is also part of the wider conversation, although his age, contract commitments, and recent performances could make a potential trade more complicated.Bryan Rust and Rickard Rakell add to trade speculationBryan Rust and Rickard Rakell are two additional Pittsburgh players reportedly available for potential trade discussions.Both forwards could attract interest from teams looking to strengthen their offensive depth before the NHL trade deadline. Their situations also reflect the possibility of a broader roster transition if Pittsburgh continues struggling.Yohe indicated that he would be surprised if at least one of the two forwards remained with the Penguins beyond the March 1 trade deadline.For now, Dubas appears prepared to let his captain determine the outcome. Whether Crosby continues in Pittsburgh, considers retirement, or explores another NHL opportunity, his wishes are expected to guide the next chapter of his career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranking Zach Werenski and the NHL Players Likely to Request a Trade Next
articles.summary: We've been reeling all season long from the number of superstar NHL players who have asked to be traded. Going back to the offseason with Connor Hellebuyck, Dylan Larkin, and now into the season with Nikita Kucherov, it's staggering to see so many elite players express displeasure with where they are and want out.
articles.body:
We've been reeling all season long from the number of superstar NHL players who have asked to be traded. Going back to the offseason with Connor Hellebuyck, Dylan Larkin, and now into the season with Nikita Kucherov, it's staggering to see so many elite players express displeasure with where they are and want out.

All while we're witnessing this change of philosophy by players and stars seeking to take control of their situations, we're left wondering: Who's next to ask for a trade?

Now that we're about 20 games into the season and we're starting to see the haves and have-nots starting to establish themselves, we're keeping our eyes fixed on the teams that are falling far back in the pack in their conferences to scout for possibilities.

Some of our choices are based on recent history, while others are tied to where their contracts are and when they're expiring. We're kicking ideas around here and wondering aloud if maybe these stars might take inspiration from current trends.

Let's explore what an Auston Matthews trade request could look like—and what it would mean for Toronto.

He is the captain of the Maple Leafs and their best player, and unfortunately, they are struggling to stay close to their rivals in the Atlantic Division and Eastern Conference yet again.

Matthews has spent several seasons on strong Toronto teams that couldn't get over the hump. Now, the Leafs face the possibility of missing the playoffs again.

Missing the playoffs would normally give Toronto the consolation of the draft lottery—the route that helped the Leafs land Gavin McKenna with the No. 1 pick in 2026. But previous trades have left them without their own first-round picks in 2027 and 2028. Add in Matthews having just one season remaining on his contract after this one before he could become an unrestricted free agent, and it's easy to see how this situation could get messy.

If Matthews requested a trade, his no-move clause would give him control over his destination. Beyond the emotional blow of losing their franchise player, the Leafs could view a deal as an opportunity to replenish their stockpile of first-round picks and top prospects—with a potentially elite successor in McKenna already on the roster.

If things keep sliding away for Toronto, you have to wonder if Matthews would want to ride it out or not. Heck, you could make the same argument for William Nylander, with the big difference being that his contract goes until 2032.

We've already seen Artemi Panarin get traded in February when the New York Rangers sent him to the Los Angeles Kings.

While Panarin enjoyed the move enough to sign a two-year extension to stay with L.A., we're guessing he wasn't expecting to see the Kings wind up near the bottom of the Western Conference when he did so.

Panarin is 35 years old, and his two-year, $22 million extension isn't exactly cheap. But given his history of offensive production and his continued solid production this season (19 points in 17 games), if he wanted to get out of Los Angeles to join a more competitive team, who could blame him?

The Kings are in a bit of an awkward transition following Anže Kopitar's retirement, with Drew Doughty at 36 years old in a contract year. They're also a very veteran team, and for the handful of top younger players they have (Quinton Byfield, Brandt Clarke), they need more. If Panarin were to ask out, trading him could help make that happen.

Pettersson's name has been in trade rumors for what feels like years. While that speculation has cooled since J.T. Miller was traded to the Rangers in January 2025, it must be tough for Pettersson to watch the Canucks struggle near the bottom of the standings yet again this season.

If Pettersson were to want out of Vancouver with five more years left on his contract with an $11.6 million cap hit, it would be equally deflating and sad to see as it would be fascinating to see how that trade would get put together.

This season, Pettersson has had a bit of a return to glory, putting up a point per game (23 points in 23 games) after producing at 0.7 points per game over the previous two seasons combined. Seeing his production pick up again despite the team's struggles is notable, especially given how much he struggled previously and how foreboding that seemed.

A Pettersson resurgence would no doubt help get more teams to the table, even with his bulky contract.

We don't mean to pick on the Canucks, but when a team has struggled as much as they have in the past few seasons and with the amount of rumors that have swirled, it's inevitable.

One of those guys who's been in rumors is Jake DeBrusk, and if the power forward wanted to escape Vancouver, there's no doubt the market for him would be busy.

DeBrusk carries a $5.5 million cap hit and a contract that has four more years beyond this one, which makes him more than affordable, especially with the cap skyrocketing in coming years. He's scored 20-plus goals in four of the past five seasons, and while he's got just 12 points in 21 games this season, his rugged style of play would make him a favorite anywhere in the league.

DeBrusk's age—30—and contract, which runs through 2031, come with the usual buyer-beware caveats. Still, his style of play and ability to get to the net would make him an attractive target.

His no-move clause this season would also allow him to pick where he wanted to go...if he wanted to leave.

There are a lot of reasons to be disappointed about seeing the Pittsburgh Penguins struggling.

Watching superstar veteran players struggle is hard, and the possibility of those players missing out on the postseason instead of getting one more crack at a Stanley Cup is sad.

While we doubt any of Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin, or Kris Letang would ask for a trade to go for a shot at one more Stanley Cup, we can't say the same for Erik Karlsson, who's still looking for his first.

Karlsson is in the final year of his contract, and even though his cap hit is still juicy at $10 million, along with a full no-move clause, he can still play well, move the puck, and produce offense from the blue line. He leads the Penguins with 19 points this season (in 20 games), with eight of those points coming on the power play.

Contending teams would love to add a player like Karlsson to make them deeper, and it's possible (likely?) that he wouldn't even need to ask for a trade to be moved this season.

GM Kyle Dubas has done well with trades the past few seasons, and if a contender calls for Karlsson, the only thing that would get in the way of him getting his asking price would be the player nixing the move.

You have to wonder what's going through Zach Werenski's mind these days.

After an awkward offseason in which he initially asked to be traded and then walked it back after speaking with Blue Jackets management, the 2026 Norris Trophy winner is playing well on a Columbus team that has sunk to the foot of the Eastern Conference.

Werenski has one more year left on his contract with the Jackets before he can become an unrestricted free agent, and with the way Columbus is struggling, you wouldn't be able to blame Werenski if he were already reassessing his desire to stay there.

An elite No. 1 defenseman hitting the trade market would create a frenzy, but Werenski's no-move clause means he would be able to select his destination of choice. Curiously enough, PuckPedia shows that Werenski's no-move changes to a 10-team trade list next season.

If Werenski says he wants out, it would create a potentially fascinating situation.

articles.title: Vale - a team who can't lose at home, can't win away
articles.summary: Port Vale are on their best winning run in 66 years at home yet have not won away from Burslem all season - are they now on the up?
articles.body:
Port Vale are truly a team in top form right now - at Vale Park, that is.

Jon Brady's side are unbeaten in 10 home league and cup games this season - the last eight of them all victories.

It is their best run in Burslem since winning 10 league and cup games on the spin between October 1960 and March 1961.

Vale have knocked in 17 goals in their past four home games, a 5-0 win against Manchester City Under-21s in the Jersey Mike's Trophy, followed by three successive 4-2s - league victories over Rochdale and Accrington Stanley, either side of knocking National League side Scunthorpe United out of the FA Cup.

After a slow start this season, 'the Brady bunch' have risen to 17th in the League Two table - and are just four points off a play-off place.

The only downside to all that positivity is that the Vale are away this Saturday, at second-placed Barnet.

And that is the flip side of this season's mathematical equations - they are currently winless in eight away league and cup games, and have picked up just one point out of a possible 18.

But in-form Vale wing-back Jaheim Headley is still hopeful Saturday might be the day when it all changes.

"Doing well away from home is how you climb the table," he told BBC Radio Stoke.

"Barnet is not an easy place to go - but we're hoping to go down there and pick up a point at least. It would show everyone how serious we are."

That sort of positive thinking is welcome news to Vale boss Brady at a time when confidence is coursing through Midlands football like a flooded river.

Four sides from the region sit in the Championship's top five, including Vale's neighbours Stoke City, while Aston Villa are on the upturn in the top flight, Crewe Alexandra and Walsall are challenging again in League Two and even freshly-purchased Shrewsbury Town are beginning to look upwards again.

"The power of the mind is just an incredible thing," Vale boss Brady told BBC Radio Stoke. "You work hard first and foremost but, if you start to believe in what you do, then, my God...

"It's the connection. People are understanding each other's games. The players really are starting to lift to the level they can be.

"There would be no bigger statement than to go and get a result at Barnet. There's no tougher place to go in the league at the moment."

Headley, with two assists in the Cup win over Scunthorpe followed by his first two goals of the season against Accrington, is arguably the best example of that.

And he puts the improvement down to working on their finishing and now taking more of their chances.

"We were having issues early on with converting our chances," he added. "We were creating chances. We just weren't converting.

"But players have taken accountability. We've been doing more on the training ground. And we've turned the corner - and everyone's contributed.

"The coaching staff always talk about playing free in the final third. And we have the players who can unlock defences.

"The fans have been great too. When the fans are behind us we're a better team. We're forever grateful to them.

"There's no better feeling as a footballer than when you're playing well."
authors: Ged Scott and Phil Bowers - BBC Sport England

articles.title: Hincapie in advanced talks over new Arsenal deal
articles.summary: Arsenal are in advanced talks with defender Piero Hincapie over a new contract.
articles.body:
Arsenal are in advanced talks with defender Piero Hincapie over a new contract.

Hincapie, 24, joined the Gunners last summer from Bayer Leverkusen, initially on loan, with the Gunners activating an option to make the move permanent at the end of the season.

The Ecuador international has established himself as a key member of Mikel Arteta's squad, making 47 appearances in all competitions.

The versatile defender's existing deal still has over four years left to run - but he is now set to sign a 12-month extension on improved terms.

Elsewhere, the club intend to open talks with left-back Riccardo Calafiori, 24, over renewing his deal.

The Italy international has become a crucial part of Arteta's plans since his arrival from Bologna in 2024.

His current deal expires in the summer of 2029, but it is expected talks over an extension will begin in the not too distant future.

Arsenal are on a contract renewal drive, with the club set to confirm new deals for Jurrien Timber, Declan Rice and goalkeeper David Raya.

articles.title: Monday Night Therapy: Ohio State is Vulnerable…But Can Nebraska Actually Win?
articles.summary: On this episode of Monday Night Therapy, Minnie Hunt and Jon Johnston welcome Ohio State insider Ramsey from Eleven Warriors for an entertaining and surprisi...
articles.body:
On this episode of Monday Night Therapy, Minnie Hunt and Jon Johnston welcome Ohio State insider Ramsey from Eleven Warriors for an entertaining and surprisingly candid preview of Nebraska's upcoming showdown with the Buckeyes.

Fresh off Nebraska's 31–0 shutout of Rutgers, the crew examines whether the Huskers can capitalize on an Ohio State team struggling with inconsistency, questionable offensive line play, defensive personnel issues, and disastrous special teams.

Ramsey pulls no punches in his assessment of the Buckeyes, discussing coaching shortcomings, transfer portal disappointments, and the challenges of starting true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey. But Ohio State still possesses one enormous advantage: superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, whom Ramsey considers the best player in college football.

The conversation also explores the changing landscape of college football, including NIL, player development, coaching stability, expanded playoffs, and whether the transfer portal has fundamentally changed the sport.

Along the way, there's plenty of good-natured trash talk, frustration with modern college football, and even some shared disdain for Michigan.

Can Nebraska build on its momentum and pull off the upset in Lincoln? Ramsey calls Saturday's matchup essentially a coin flip, giving Husker fans reason for cautious optimism.

articles.title: Abu Dhabi confirms release of Usman and Umar Nurmagomedov from prison
articles.summary: Usman Nurmagomedov and Umar Nurmagomedov have been released from Abu Dhabi jail just days after receiving six month sentences for attacking former UFC bantam...
articles.body:
Usman Nurmagomedov and Umar Nurmagomedov have been released from Abu Dhabi jail just days after receiving six month sentences for attacking former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili.

Usman Nurmagomedov, the PFL lightweight champion, was in Abu Dhabi to support his brother Umar in his Real American Freestyle match against Urijah Faber. He got a little sidetracked on that front when he and several teammates spotted Dvalishvili at the athlete hotel and jumped him. Footage of the brawl quickly hit the internet, and just as quickly everyone involved was arrested by Abu Dhabi authorities.

Six month sentences and $82,000 fines were issued to the eight men who instigated the attack. Four days later, a deal was reached to reduce the sentences and deport them with $41,000 fines. We're still sorting out just what happened … there are reports that Khabib Nurmagomedov travelled to Abu Dhabi to secure the release of his cousins and teammates, other reports of million dollar payments behind the scenes, and even more whispers of a gag order to never speak of the incident in public.

None of that is confirmed. But Abu Dhabi authorities did release a statement confirming the release for totally legitimate reasons.

"The Criminal Court has reduced the sentences of eight defendants involved in a mass brawl at a hotel, filming it and causing public disorder following earlier disputes between them," the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department statement read. "The revised penalty is a fine of Dh150,000 for each defendant, following reconciliation and mutual withdrawal of claims between the parties, as well as an appeal by the victim to the Abu Dhabi Government for their release."

The two victims of the attack, Merab Dvalishvili and Saba Lazishvili, both refused to press charges and repeatedly called for the release of the men who attacked them. That seems to have played a big part in allowing Abu Dhabi to show leniency to Team Nurmagomedov.

"The ruling is consistent with the legal framework governing the criminal case and considers the settlement between the parties and their withdrawal of mutual claims and disputes arising from the incident."

This is a big win for Usman and Umar Nurmagomedov, whose careers were looking like they'd be badly derailed due to their thuggish stupidity. Six months in prison would have screwed up their year, not to mention the possibility of being barred from entering the U.A.E. and possibly other countries due to criminal charges.

We'll keep you updated as further details emerge from the situation.

articles.title: Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle reunites with family and close friends during Edmonton Oilers’ NHL game against Maple Leafs
articles.summary: Lauren Kyle McDavid enjoyed a heartwarming reunion with family and friends during the Edmonton Oilers' 1-0 victory against the Toronto Maple Leafs, showcasing deep personal ties and an impressive performance from her husband, Connor McDavid.
articles.body: Connor McDavid’s wife, Lauren Kyle McDavid, attended the Edmonton Oilers’ 1-0 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs at Scotiabank Arena on Saturday, November 14. She watched the NHL matchup from the family press box, joined by relatives and longtime friends.The Toronto visit was also an opportunity for Lauren to spend time with people close to the couple. Her group included Connor McDavid’s brother Cameron and his wife Sarah, as well as Rachel Gagner, wife of former Edmonton Oilers forward Sam Gagner.Lauren Kyle McDavid at Edmonton Oilers-Toronto Maple Leafs gameLauren watched the game alongside Rachel Gagner and her son, along with Cameron McDavid and his wife, Sarah. The gathering brought together family members and friends who have maintained close connections with the McDavid family over the years.Rachel Gagner and Lauren have shared a friendship for several years. Rachel was also among the friends who joined Lauren for her bachelorette trip to France in 2024, ahead of her wedding to Connor McDavid in Muskoka.Their reunion in Toronto therefore offered more than an opportunity to watch an NHL game. It brought together familiar faces while Connor and the Edmonton Oilers competed in an important regular-season matchup.How did the Toronto visit extend beyond the NHL game?The visit included time with Connor McDavid's family away from Scotiabank Arena. Lauren's social media post about the short trip featured a video of her brother-in-law during a music performance she attended while in Toronto.She also spent time with her in-laws at a private gathering alongside her husband. Her Toronto appearance also highlighted the connections the McDavid family maintains in the region, particularly given Connor's background in the Greater Toronto Area.The family gathering coincided with an important night for Connor McDavid and the Edmonton Oilers. Playing at Scotiabank Arena therefore offers an opportunity to compete in front of family, friends and fans who have followed his career since his early years.His return to Toronto combined a personal connection with another strong performance for Edmonton. articles.standfirst: Estos son los favoritos para Codere para hacerse con el trofeo nacional
articles.summary: Estos son los favoritos para Codere para hacerse con el trofeo nacional
articles.body: La primera ronda de la Copa del Rey está a punto de echar el cierre, con algunos partidos aplazados que se disputan hasta este miércoles 18. Ha dejado la habitual cosecha de goleadas y sorpresas, como la eliminación del Oviedo ante el Numancia en los penaltis o el 4-3 del Sestao River al Espanyol en la prórroga. Mientras tanto, los cuatro participantes de la Supercopa (Barcelona, Real Madrid, Atlético y Real Sociedad) esperan sentados a los dieciseisavos del 16 de diciembre. Con ese panorama, Codere ya ha actualizado su mercado de apuestas deportivas para el título. El Barcelona es el gran favorito, a cuota 2.6. Los azulgranas llegan como líderes de LaLiga y con la maquinaria ofensiva más productiva del campeonato, aunque acaban de caer en el Clásico ante el Real Madrid. Esa derrota no ha movido su cuota, que implica una probabilidad cercana al 38%. El mercado entiende que su plantilla tiene recursos de sobra para afrontar un torneo de partidos únicos, aunque el año pasado se quedó en las semifinales, eliminado por el Atlético. El Real Madrid aparece segundo, a cuota 3.75. Los blancos ganaron el Clásico, llegan tras una racha de victorias consecutivas y, como el resto de la élite, no entrarán en juego hasta diciembre. Su cuota refleja la jerarquía de un equipo capaz de imponerse en cualquier escenario, pero también cierta irregularidad como visitante, un factor que pesa en una competición donde se juega siempre en el campo del rival más modesto hasta las semifinales. El Atlético de Madrid se paga a 6.5. Fue finalista el año pasado y perdió la final ante la Real Sociedad en los penaltis, después de un 2-2 que obligó a jugar la prórroga. Su cuota premia a un equipo que sabe lo que significa llegar hasta el final de este torneo y que cuenta con un técnico, Simeone, que ha convertido las eliminatorias en su especialidad. A cuota 6.5, el mercado lo ve como la alternativa más atractiva en la relación entre riesgo y recompensa. La Real Sociedad defiende título y cotiza a 15. Los donostiarras, campeones tras superar al Atlético en La Cartuja, saltan al torneo en los dieciseisavos y su cuota refleja las dudas sobre su capacidad para repetir con una plantilla menos profunda que la de los tres favoritos. Es una opción que quedará condicionada por el sorteo y por su rendimiento en los próximos meses. El Betis cierra la lista, a cuota 17. Ha superado su estreno copero este mismo mes tras remontarle el Navalcarnero y necesitar la prórroga para pasar de ronda, un recordatorio de lo peligroso que es este torneo para los equipos de Primera. Los verdiblancos, campeones en 2022, mantienen la ilusión con un arranque de Champions de tres victorias en tres jornadas, aunque su cuota advierte de que el título exigiría una carrera casi perfecta. Estos son los principales favoritos para las casas de apuestas, en concreto, para Codere.

articles.title: Week 11 Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Pickups: Kaelon Black among top adds with 6 teams on bye, rash of injuries
articles.summary: Boone goes over his top waiver wire adds at each position going into Week 11 of the fantasy football season.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

The Titans are pushing the pace on offense and are using a no-huddle approach at one of the highest rates in the league. That's helped Ward to his two best fantasy results of the season in the last two games, finishing as the QB4 in Week 8 and coming off the bye as the QB12 in Week 10.

Ward has also done this without his top receiver Carnell Tate, who's missed the last two outings but is expected to return for their Week 11 matchup with the Cowboys. It's the right time to get back since Tennessee is third in neutral pace of play and Dallas leads the league in that category — setting up a massive opportunity for fantasy scoring.

It's also worth noting that Ward has one of the five easiest fantasy schedules for QBs the rest of the way, including matchups with the Commanders (Week 13), Lions (Week 14), Colts (Week 15) and Raiders (Week 16). Though I'm still only valuing Ward as a fantasy QB2 streamer, don't be surprised if we see the former first-round pick finish hot down the stretch.

Desperation streaming options (if starter is out)

Black has been one of the stars of this column all season long and the fact that he's still available in over 60% of fantasy leagues is a massive mistake by managers.

Just look at what happened with Emmett Johnson last week, when Kenneth Walker III got hurt in practice. The Chiefs' rookie stepped into the starting role and delivered 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. That's the kind of upside Black offers if Christian McCaffrey were ever to miss time.

Even with CMC active, Black's role has grown in recent weeks resulting in 59 yards and TD in Week 7, a bye in Week 8, 70 yards in Week 9 and 68 yards and a TD last week. Most importantly, he's been given at least 11 touches in each of those games. When you're playing in one of the best offenses in the NFL, that kind of volume makes you a strong RB3/flex option with weekly RB2 upside when you find the end zone.

Don't let Black remain on the waiver wire any longer, he should be rostered in 100% of leagues.

Baker Mayfield is banged up and might sit out this week, which would put Jalon Daniels back under center. The rookie performed well in his three starts earlier in the season, but be prepared for the Bucs offense to lean even heavier on the run.

Gainwell has displayed weekly RB3/flex value over the last three games with 88 yards in Week 7, 140 yards in Week 8 and 76 yards in Week 9 before the team went on bye.

Bucky Irving is the unquestioned starter in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell needs to be rostered everywhere as a flex option with RB1 upside if injuries strike.

Even after a potential Jonathan Taylor trade failed to materialize, the Colts continued to split RB volume with the veteran turning his 18 touches into 103 scrimmage yards and McGowan chipping in with 77 yards and a TD on 12 opportunities.

It's the second consecutive game where the rookie reached the end zone, making him a legitimate RB3/flex option in fantasy, even as Taylor's running mate.

We could also see the team shut Taylor down at some point in the final two months, if he gets even the slightest injury. There's no reason to risk your star on a team that's going nowhere. If that occurs, McGowan would be a fantasy RB2 in whatever games he starts.

Woody Marks suffered a concussion and is unlikely to be cleared before Thursday's game against the Colts. David Montgomery, who hasn't suited up since Week 5 due to a groin injury, returned to practice last week and put in a full session on Friday, but was ultimately ruled out for the game. That puts Montgomery on track to potentially play against the Colts, unless he suffered a setback.

If Montgomery can't go, then Demercado would be the next man up. He's earned 15 touches while playing behind Marks the last two games, only managing 39 scoreless scrimmage yards. In that scenario, Demercado would be a volume-based fantasy RB3.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt is 52% rostered but would be the No. 3 RB add, if available.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. at NYG (37% rostered)

It's easy to forget, but Bryant had a growing role in the Broncos' passing attack during the opening month before being placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury. In those first four games, Bryant topped 40 yards three times.

So, it was great to see him post a season-high 56 yards and a touchdown on four catches in his first game back since the injury. Jaylen Waddle also suffered a concussion, but he should be cleared coming off Denver's Week 10 bye.

Regardless, Bryant was a borderline flex option early in the season and has returned with an even better performance. Given Waddle's struggles and Courtland Sutton's age, there's a non-zero chance Bryant becomes the most valuable fantasy receiver in Denver for the rest of the season.

While CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens get all the headlines, Flournoy has become a very consistent contributor in the Cowboys' passing attack.

The 27-year-old has at least 50 yards and/or a touchdown in six straight games, finishing as a top-24 fantasy WR in five of those outings.

Even as the third pass-catcher in Dallas, Flournoy can be started in fantasy as a WR3/flex option, especially in an uptempo contest against a Titans defense allowing the most points to wideouts.

Despite not earning the kind of volume we'd like to see from a full-time receiver, Williams has been productive most weeks. The rookie has at least 50 yards or a touchdown in three of his last four games since Terry McLaurin was lost for the season.

Until he sees more consistent targets, it's hard to trust Williams as anything more than a flex option. However, his schedule is favorable in the coming weeks with the Bengals, Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons. With Stefon Diggs drawing the attention of top corners, Williams could earn more volume during that span.

Mitchell's outlook is complicated. Omar Cooper Jr. is dealing with an ankle injury that could sideline him for a few games. That would condense the crowded receiver room down to Mitchell and Garrett Wilson, making Mitchell a possible WR3/flex option in fantasy.

Unfortunately, Geno Smith also suffered an ankle injury that might sideline him. Rookie backup Cade Klubnik represents a significant downgrade that would lower the ceiling of all the skill positions players in New York's offense.

So, Mitchell is a tentative add who could be started if Cooper misses time and if Smith doesn't. The fact that I'm writing about him in the waiver wire column is a clear sign we've reached Week 11 and the pickups are getting thin.

Jordyn Tyson is 58% rostered but would be the No. 1 WR add, if available.

Keenan Allen is 59% rostered but would be the No. 2 WR add behind Tyson, if available.

Tank Dell is 51% rostered but would be the No. 6 WR add behind Tyson, Allen, Flournoy, Williams and Mitchell, if available.

Khalil Shakir is 59% rostered but would be the No. 7 WR add behind Tyson, Allen, Flournoy, Williams, Mitchell and Dell, if available.

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

Brock Bowers hurt his ankle on Sunday, but thankfully the team believes he avoided a major injury and should return "sooner rather than later."

Whether that means he'll be ready for their Week 11 date with the Broncos, remains to be seen.

Denver is one of the five easiest matchups for fantasy tight ends, so Mayer would immediately be in the streamer mix if he's called upon to start.

Since McLaurin's season-ending injury, Okonkwo has averaged the ninth-most targets among tight ends and turned in three games with over 50 yards in five outings.

Okonkwo was well on his way to a much bigger day this past week, but his ongoing back injury caused him to miss part of the contest. With Okonkwo not playing his usual snaps, backup Ben Sinnott turned in four catches, 42 yards and a touchdown.

As long as he stays healthy, Okonkwo has moved into the high-end TE2 streamer conversation, with a chance to crack the low-end TE1 range moving forward.

Mark Andrews is 53% rostered but would be the No. 3 TE add behind Mayer and Okonkwo, if available.

Chiefs defense is 58% rostered but would be the No. 1 DEF add, if available.

Quarterbacks: Lamar Jackson, Aaron Rodgers

Running Backs: Tyler Allgeier, J.K. Dobbins, TreVeyon Henderson, Corey Kiner

Wide Receivers: A.J. Brown, Germie Bernard, DeMario Douglas, Xavier Worthy

Aside from taking advantage of the Cowboys defense in Week 8, Allgeier has struggled to make his mark with Jeremiyah Love on IR. Allgeier only managed 46 yards on 19 touches in Week 9 and turned his five carries into 14 yards on Sunday. With so many injuries to the Cardinals offense, Allgeier isn't likely to provide much value moving forward.

The Patriots have lost Drake Maye for an extended stretch and possibly the rest of the season . That's why you see so many Pats in the drop section, including Brown (who's hurt as well), Douglas, Henderson, Kiner and Henry. There's very little value in New England with Tommy DeVito slated to start when they return from their Week 11 bye.

Since his back to back 80-yard games a month ago, Bernard has failed to top 30 yards in any of his past three outings. With Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson eventually returning, Bernard can be dropped in favor of a pickup who offers more upside.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on AJ Lee's Return, Kasper Brothers' AEW Debut Reaction and Stephanie Vaquer on SmackDown
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.

Predicting Final Members of Team USA and Team Mexico 🔮

Having been off WWE television since WrestleMania, AJ Lee is reportedly not expected to be back before the end of the year.

In a recent Q&A session with WrestleVotes (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), Joey Votes wrote the "best-case scenario" for AJ returning would be at the Royal Rumble.

"Will AJ Lee wrestle again this year? No," Votes wrote. "Best-case scenario is her showing up at the Royal Rumble, so that's in 2027. So no, she won't wrestle again this year."

AJ's final match to this point was against Becky Lynch at WrestleMania 42. The Man defeated AJ to win the women's intercontinental championship.

Following the match, AJ indicated in a post on Instagram (h/t SI.com's Rick Ucchino ) she would be stepping away but left the door open for something in the future.

"Thank you for supporting me for two decades, selling out my merchandise, giving me record-setting views, and making Converse a small fortune with your AJ cosplay," she wrote. "Your passion kept me coming back. Stay weird, see you soon."

If AJ is going to wrestle again, the Royal Rumble would be an ideal event to return given WWE likes to include surprise entrants in the match.

AJ returned to WWE in September 2025, more than 10 years after her initial retirement. She went on to wrestle five matches as part of her comeback, including the women's WarGames match at Survivor Series and defeating Lynch to win the intercontinental title at Elimination Chamber.

WWE Reaction to Kasper Brothers' AEW Debut

The Kasper Brothers, formerly known as the Creed Brothers, became the latest former WWE stars to make the jump to AEW when they debuted at Full Gear on Saturday night.

Per WrestleVotes in a Q&A session (h/t Upton ), WWE is aware that talent will look to AEW as an alternative and WWE's mentality toward contracts is informed by various metrics being studied:

"When WWE starts to say, 'All right, we're gonna get rid of our left-handed pitching,' AEW's right there to pick up that left-handed pitching. ... It's the case with the tag teams. WWE is saying, 'The New Day, as much as you guys have drawn and merchandise, the market right now is not really indicating to us it's worth bringing you in.' There's AEW — pick 'em up. Same with the Creed Brothers. Their contracts expire, AEW picks them up. "

Word came out on Nov. 6 that the former Julius and Brutus Creed were no longer in WWE when their profiles were moved the alumni section on the company's website.

The speculation was confirmed on Saturday when the brothers — now using their real names, Jacob and Drew Kasper — aligned with FTR by attacking the Motor City Machine Guns and Young Bucks after the latter duo successfully defended the AEW tag team titles by defeating Davis and Doyle.

AEW is a better fit for the Kaspers primarily because its tag division is stronger and there's more investment in tag team wrestling than in WWE.

The Penta-Je'Von Evans victory over The Vision to win the world tag titles at Crown Jewel on Nov. 7 marked the first time the titles have been defended a premium live event since WrestleMania 41 in April 2025.

Working in AEW gives the Kasper Brothers a chance to work with the Bucks, FTR, Motor City Machine Guns, Kofi and Austin Creed, Brodido, any two members of the Death Riders and The Conglomeration, among many others.

Even though Stephanie Vaquer has officially been a member of the Raw roster since May 2025, her return after a brief absence last week came on SmackDown.

Per WrestleVotes (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), WWE wanted to put Vaquer on SmackDown to keep her separate from Becky and Liv Morgan as they feud over the women's world title for the time being.

"They are going to be avoiding each other now that Stephanie Vaquer showed up on SmackDown unannounced," WrestleVotes wrote. "It's just a way to get her away from the RAW title scene until they want her back."

La Primera had been feuding with both Morgan and Lynch, highlighted by Vaquer beating Morgan for the championship at a house show in Chile with Becky serving as special referee.

Morgan regained the title at Money in the Bank in a triple-threat match with Lynch and Vaquer when she pinned Vaquer.

Lynch and Morgan will have a one-on-one encounter for the world championship at Survivor Series. Vaquer had been absent from television for about a month before returning on SmackDown to help Charlotte defeat Jacy Jayne.

Vaquer will team with Charlotte, Bayley, Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley against Fatal Influence and Michin in the women's WarGames match at Survivor Series.

articles.title: College Basketball Catchup: Thriving UCLA, Bobcats Turnover, Moreno Does It All
articles.summary: UCLA is looking great, Kentucky bounced back, one player did it all and more from Monday's college basketball action.
articles.body: UCLA keeps pouring on the 100s. Kentucky bounces back thanks to a 7-footer. Michigan is going to be a problem. Here's what you need to know from Monday's slate of college basketball. One Name To Know: Eric Dailey Jr. No. 7 UCLA is off to a great start this season, as the Bruins aren’t just winning in the early going but decimating opponents. The year began with a win against Arizona, and UCLA followed that ranked-ranked upset W with three-straight 100-plus point games, the latest a 105-66 win over Long Beach State on Monday. Among the keys to that victory was senior forward Eric Dailey Jr., whose numbers are up across the board in the early going. His 25 points matched a career high, and he started early with a 3 to make it 7-2 just over three minutes in — UCLA never looked back. Dailey shot under 49% in 2025-2026, but is at 53.2% to this point this season, and his points per game have jumped from 11.6 to 15.5. He’s also averaging what would be career bests in rebounds (7.0), assists (2.8), blocks (0.5) and steals (1.5) — yes, Dailey and UCLA are just four games in, but this is a great start for both, and if Dailey can keep it up, then it will be easier for UCLA to do the same. Top Performance: Malachi Moreno Kentucky hasn’t exactly been covering itself in glory lately — the Wildcats got booted from the latest Associated Press top 25 after escaping Northern Arizona thanks more to the Lumberbacks losing the game on missed free throws rather than Kentucky winning it — but Monday represented a step in the right direction. The Wildcats crushed Grambling State 88-59, and seven-foot sophomore Malachi Moreno was at the center of that successful performance. He scored 22 points while pulling down 12 rebounds — six offensive, six defensive — and added one assist, four steals and three blocks. The 22 points led all scorers, as did the rebounds and steals, and the blocks were tied for a game-high. Moreno has seen a huge jump in performance early on, even if Kentucky as a whole hasn’t impressed, increasing his rebounds from 6.3 per game to 9, his points from 7.8 to 14.2, assists from 1.8 to 3.2 and a jump in shooting percentage from 58.2% to 66.7%. Kentucky still has issues to solve — a one-game win over Northern Arizona is troubling, and it took more time than it should have to create separation from Grambling State in the follow-up contest — but more performances like this one from Moreno will change the Wildcats’ fortunes. Get To Know A Mid-Major: Quinnipiac Quinnipiac’s women’s team was on the bubble last year after becoming regular-season conference champs but losing to Fairfield in the Metro — née MAAC — conference title game, and has a new coach this season after Tricia Fabbri retired at the end of the year. Roman Owen took over a squad with just three returning players from that regular-season championship, and the Bobcats got back to .500 with a non-conference win against the Yale Bulldogs on Monday. Lilly Thomas, new to this year's roster, led the way: the sophomore center scored 22 points on 11-for-14 shooting while grabbing eight boards and blocked a pair of shots — no small thing in a 59-53 victory. Shooting 78% was also huge, considering Quinnipiac shot just 42% as a team even with that in the mix. The Bobcats are basically starting over in 2026-2027, given the massive roster turnover and new coach, but it’s also the last year in which back-to-back-to-back champs Fairfield are in the Metro before a move to the Coastal Athletic Association in 2027 — this is a transitional season for Quinnipiac, but also for the conference as a whole. Men's Scoring Leader: Karris Bilal It didn’t help Texas Southern defeat UC San Diego — the Tritons would win, 97-92 — but Karris Bilal made it close thanks to 36 points. It wasn’t just the points, either, as the sophomore guard also grabbed eight rebounds and dished out three assists in 39 minutes. Those 36 points led all Division I men’s hoopers on Monday, and in fact was one of just two 30-point games across the league. Women's Scoring Leader: Kailyn Gilbert Senior guard Kailyn Gilbert had a monster game for Texas A&M, but to understand just how significant it was you need to see how many points the Aggies scored as a whole. Texas A&M scored 61 in a win over Lamar, and Gilbert dropped 32 of those points — more than half of her team’s scoring. Gilbert also added four rebounds, two assists and three steals to her stat sheet, and turned the ball over just once while shooting 3-for-5 from deep, hitting all five shots from the line and going 12-for-22 overall. A highly efficient, productive game, and an absolutely necessary performance, with the rest of the Aggies managing 29 combined points and shooting all of 43% even with her night included. Before You Go: Michigan Is Terrifying Michigan is looking terrifying. Defeating Central Michigan 101-30 isn’t necessarily a sign on its own that the Wolverines are a terror, but you can still see ways in which this might be a better team than last season’s squad. Michigan shot 52% as a whole, and 38% on 3-pointers — if the Wolverines are making better decisions on shots rather than rushing them, which was a huge problem for a team that occasionally looked its youthful age a year ago, then it will be more difficult to stop them in 2026-2027. And even more difficult to stop Michigan if its relentless defense continues to punish opponents, flooding shooting lanes with bodies and cutting off opportunities for easy scores. In a related story, Central Michigan shot just 21% overall, making 12 field goals, and were 4-for-29 from beyond the arc. The Wolverines more than doubled up Central Michigan on rebounds, 54 to 23, and forced 28 turnovers, scoring 41 points off those. Again, Central Michigan isn’t the most challenging opponent for a team of Michigan’s stature, but the Wolverines’ problems from a year ago haven’t been showing up against any opposition yet, not just the ones that are supposed to be easy dubs. There’s a reason Michigan is No. 2, and also reasons to believe that it’ll stay near the top of the rankings for some time. articles.title: Charlie Woods faces constant Tiger Woods comparisons: How Florida State University recruit navigates expectations, public scrutiny and pressure to build his own identity in junior golf
articles.summary: Explore how Charlie Woods, son of golf legend Tiger Woods, is building his own identity in junior golf amid scrutiny and comparisons, as he signs with Florida State University for collegiate competition.
articles.body: Charlie Woods has been around the game of golf his whole life, but being the son of Tiger Woods comes with expectations that few young athletes face. Every tournament appearance, every shot, every on-course mannerism is noticed. Fans often compare the teenager to his father, one of the greatest golfers in history.At 17, Charlie is at a major juncture in his development, and he has officially signed with Florida State University for the Class of 2027. His father's achievements are an unavoidable part of the story, but the young golfer is starting to build a competitive career of his own, through junior tournaments, school golf, and his own decisions.Why Charlie Woods faces more pressure than Tiger WoodsThe comparisons between Tiger Woods and Charlie Woods are easy to see, given they share the same surname, play similar styles, and have both dabbled in competitive golf early on. But the expectations of the younger Woods are considerably different from those his father had as a teenager. Tiger made his name in an era when junior golf wasn’t covered as extensively online, allowing young players more privacy between tournaments.But Charlie plays in an environment in which almost every big moment can be a social media discussion. His performances are often recorded and passed around, compared to footage of his father. Even the mundane stuff, like club twirls, tee pickups, and reactions after shots, draws attention for its resemblance to Tiger's mannerisms.Another reason why comparisons have become hard to avoid is Tiger's junior career. And while he already has some big wins under his belt, expecting him to replicate his father’s feats at the same age ignores the differences in their situations and personal growth.It’s not just Charlie’s tournament performance that has drawn him attention. The appearances with Tiger at the PNC Championship gave golf fans a look at their relationship and similarities in their games. Since then, video of the father-son duo has often garnered interest, making Charlie a familiar face even to fans who don’t closely follow junior golf.The problem is, comparing yourself to a 15-time major champion can mess up the progress of any young golfer. Charlie’s progress should be measured on its own terms, not on the assumption that he will one day equal Tiger’s professional record.Tiger Woods explains modern junior golf scrutiny facing Charlie WoodsTiger Woods has confessed that his son's experience is not the same as his own. Ahead of the 2024 PNC Championship, the former world No. 1 said social media, smartphones and the ubiquity of video recording have changed how young golfers handle public attention.Tiger said his junior tournaments weren’t videotaped the same way. While he also drew attention in his teenage years, the coverage was largely different from the continuous exposure Charlie experiences today.In December 2020, in comments reported by GOLF.com, Tiger discussed how spectators now have the ability to record almost every moment. He also said that Charlie was used to playing junior tournaments with people filming him.That difference became more significant as Charlie began competing in more competitive tournaments. He played in the U.S. Junior Amateur and other top junior tournaments and drew more than the usual following for those events.The pressure isn’t just on spectators or social media chatter. Expectations are also a factor in the athlete’s mindset in competition, especially when every performance is being compared to the successes of the parent.Charlie Woods faces expectations beyond tournament resultsThe attention the public is giving Charlie also reflects the wider interest in Tiger Woods’ family. Naturally, fans want to know if the younger golfer has the potential to make it to the pro level.And while comparisons are inevitable, Charlie has carved out his own path in golf with individual success and high school tournaments. He’s won tournaments, played well against proven junior competition, and is still making his mark in amateur golf. He closed with rounds of 70, 65, and 66 to win by three shots for his first AJGA title.The win was a significant milestone because it showed he can go against a strong junior field. It also gave him an accomplishment that could be judged separately from his father's pro career.Charlie has also been part of The Benjamin School’s success in Florida high school golf. Adding to his experience in team competitions, he helped the team win the 2023 and 2025 Florida High School Athletic Association Class 1A state championships.He posted another strong result in September 2026 at The Junior PLAYERS Championship at TPC Sawgrass. Charlie tied for eighth at the finish, shooting 71, 73, and 71 to end the tournament one-under-par.Florida State University becomes Charlie Woods' next destinationCharlie took a huge step toward collegiate golf in November 2026 when he signed his athletic grant-in-aid agreement with Florida State University. He will join head coach Trey Jones and the Seminoles in front of the 2027-28 season.This decision is interesting because his father, Tiger Woods, played collegiate golf at Stanford University, where he had a good amount of success. By choosing Florida State, Charlie gets a chance to create his own college experience instead of following his dad's institutional footsteps.He will also join a highly regarded recruiting class that includes Miles Russell, one of the top junior golfers in the country. Florida State announced the signings of Russell, Charlie Woods, Kaden Puranik and Edwin Askerfors, staying with the program with a top-rated incoming group.Can Charlie Woods develop beyond his father's shadow?Plenty of time for Charlie to grow before he starts collegiate competition. He will have the opportunity to raise his game at Florida State, playing against high-level players and gaining experience within a structured college golf program.Tiger’s impact will always be a part of Charlie’s journey, especially since they share a love for the game. But the younger Woods has already proven he’s had his own accomplishments and decisions in his career.His biggest challenge is to balance the attention of his family name and still enjoy playing competitive golf right now. His decision to sign with Florida State is a clean slate, a chance to build his reputation on his own merits instead of always being measured against one of the game’s all-time greats.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Last season, May posted a combined 7-9 record with a 4.70 ERA, 1.32 WHIP, and 144 strikeouts across 145 ⅔ innings pitched, while bouncing between the starting rotation and bullpen during Milwaukee’s World Series run. While May's inconsistent production makes him a bit of a gamble for the White Sox, he also offers a durable, back-of-the-rotation presence and provides an experienced starter for a young Chicago starting rotation. The 29-year-old May joins a rotation that projects to include Sean Burke, Grant Taylor, Davis Martin, and Anthony Kay, while young left-handers Hagen Smith and Noah Schultz should also see expanded roles in 2027. May spent the first six-plus years of his MLB career with the Los Angeles Dodgers before being traded to the Boston Red Sox during the 2025 MLB season and then signing a one-year deal with the Cardinals in the ensuing offseason.

articles.title: Ice hockey Federation's Website Hacked After Russia's Removal from World Juniors
articles.summary: ZURICH (AP) — The website of the International Ice Hockey Federation was offline Tuesday after what it called a cyberattack amid disputes over the IIHF's decision to remove Russia from the world junior championship.
articles.body:
ZURICH (AP) — The website of the International Ice Hockey Federation was offline Tuesday after what it called a cyberattack amid disputes over the IIHF's decision to remove Russia from the world junior championship.

An image of Russian players briefly appeared alongside a message accusing the federation of banning a team its opponents couldn't beat, the Canadian Press reported.

Later Tuesday, the website only displayed a message stating it was "temporarily unavailable" during maintenance.

"The International Ice Hockey Federation has been the target of a cyberattack," the IIHF said in a statement on X. "We strongly condemn these actions and are taking all necessary steps to investigate the source of the attack and restore our systems. Our platforms will be back online as soon as we are confident they are secure. The IIHF remains committed to protecting the integrity of our organization and safeguarding our sport."

The Russian Ice Hockey Federation condemned the hacker attack and said Russia's case for competing should only be made using lawful means.

"The RIHF views such actions negatively and considers the use of abusive methods to express a sporting or public stance to be unacceptable," the Russian hockey federation added. "Furthermore, the RIHF does not condone interference with information resources or any actions that fall outside the legal framework."

Russia won't compete at the world junior hockey championship starting next month because of tournament host Canada's decision to bar Russian players, the IIHF said Sunday. The Canadian government said it would not allow Russia's team to compete following a Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling late last month that reinstated Russia in IIHF events.

articles.title: Charlotte Flair faces criticism over her famous surname: How Ric Flair's daughter overcame expectations to prove herself and build an independent WWE legacy
articles.summary: Discover how Charlotte Flair, daughter of wrestling legend Ric Flair, overcame the shadows of her famous surname to build her own independent legacy in WWE, proving herself through perseverance and determination.
articles.body: Charlotte Flair is one of the most decorated women superstars in WWE history, but her climb to the top has been about more than just titles. In a 2026 interview with No-Contest Wrestling, she said she felt guilty because she didn’t go the “traditional” route of getting a WWE tryout.She explained that watching other female wrestlers struggle to secure opportunities made her feel that she needed to work harder to justify her position. The criticism surrounding her family name also contributed to the pressure.Charlotte admitted in a previous interview with Muscle & Fitness that her dad’s name helped open the door. She stressed, though, that she didn’t just fall into opportunities and championship victories.Her own essay in The Players’ Tribune, Letter to My Dad, also touched on her early fears of not living up to the extraordinary legacy of Ric Flair.Charlotte Flair builds her own WWE championship legacyLittle by little, Charlotte’s work inside the WWE began to make a strong case against those who questioned her credentials as a wrestler. She debuted in NXT in July 2013 and won her first NXT Women's Championship on May 29, 2014, by defeating Natalya.2015 was another big chapter in her main-roster arrival. She then made her name in the women’s division, winning titles and fighting in historic bouts.She won the Royal Rumble in 2025, which was big, especially as she had been away for a long time due to a knee injury. She became the first woman to win the Women’s Royal Rumble twice, cementing her legacy in WWE history.Ric Flair’s support shapes Charlotte Flair’s perspectiveBut for all the comparisons, Charlotte has never quite escaped her father’s shadow. Instead, she has slowly learned to embrace the connection without letting it define her professional identity.She has spoken in interviews about how personal growth and experience helped her stop feeling apologetic about being Ric Flair's daughter. Also, she admitted that her father was a big help in motivating her wrestling aspirations.Charlotte has grown in her response to criticism over time. The actress has spent her time not trying to prove to everyone that she deserves to be there, but instead trying to improve her acting and develop a unique character.And her evolution into The Queen also allowed her to take on a confident, commanding presence on screen. The character became such a huge part of her identity, separating her wrestling self from her life outside of the ring.In the end, Charlotte Flair’s journey demonstrates that a famous wrestling name can be a blessing and an added pressure. Ric Flair’s influence is still part of her story, but her championship credentials and in-ring work have created her own legacy in WWE.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vitality Roses: Alicia Scholes ruled out for the season with Olivia Tchine and Sasha Glasgow out of Jamaica games
articles.summary: Vitality Roses head coach Anna Stembridge has been hit by multiple injuries ahead of her side's upcoming Vitality Netball Horizon Series against Jamaica; Alicia Scholes will miss the remainder of the season, while Olivia Tchine and Sasha Glasgow will not make the series
articles.body:
England Netball say Scholes, who is the daughter of Manchester United great Paul Scholes, will commence her rehabilitation immediately and will be supported by both the governing body and London Pulse's medical and performance teams.

"We're all gutted for Alicia," Roses head coach Anna Stembridge said, as she unveiled her squads for her side's upcoming Vitality Netball Horizon Series on Tuesday.

"She's been working incredibly hard in camp, and it's been great to see her developing combinations and making her mark within the group.

"To have her season end this way is hugely disappointing, but she has the full support of both England Netball and London Pulse as she begins her rehabilitation."

Stembridge also announced Olivia Tchine and Sasha Glasgow had been omitted from both home and away squads for her side's upcoming Vitality Netball Horizon Series due to injury.

The series will see the Roses face Jamaica on November 21 and 22 in a two-match series at London's Copper Box Arena, before travelling to face the same opponent in the away leg in Kingston on December 5 and 6.

Nat Metcalf, Ella Clark and Berri Neal have all been drafted into the squad. Metcalf returns to the court after sustaining an injury at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

Neal will act as a travelling reserve for both home and away legs, while Clark, who made her Commonwealth Games debut in the summer, will be included in the full squad for the opening match, before also moving to become a second travelling reserve for the second match.

Izzi Phillips, who had previously been a travelling reserve for the away leg, has been elevated to the squad for the full series.

Vice-captain Tchine suffered an injury in October and will miss the series as she completes her return-to-play protocols.

Glasgow had picked up her injury in training before coming into camp, and will miss the home leg of the series, before joining the squad in Jamaica for the final two matches.

Stembridge said: "It's never easy to lose players through injury, particularly at this stage of our preparations.

"Liv [Olivia Tchine] and Sasha [Glasgow] both need a little more time in their return-to-play journeys, and we'll continue to support them as they work towards getting back on court."

Reflecting on her injury, Tchine said: "I'm absolutely gutted to not be playing in the Vitality Netball Horizon Series this year.

"Just like every other England game, I was looking forward to playing against some of the world's best players. Injuries are annoying and frustrating but I'm working so hard to make sure that I'm back on court for the next series.

"In the meantime, I'll be the Vitality Roses' biggest and LOUDEST cheerleader, supporting them all the way!"
