articles.summary: José Escorcia suena con fuerza para llegar al equipo italiano
articles.body: El mercado de fichajes internacional no descansa y los focos del Viejo Continente vuelven a posarse sobre el fútbol colombiano. La capacidad del balompié nacional para formar talento joven y proyectarlo hacia las ligas más competitivas del planeta sigue vigentes. En las últimas semanas, un nombre procedente de las divisiones menores y del primer equipo de Atlético Nacional ha comenzado a sonar con fuerza en las oficinas de los principales V.I.P. del fútbol italiano, apuntando directamente al radar de un histórico gigante como el Milan. La noticia, que han publicado medios como la Gazzetta dello Sport en Italia, ha generado enorme expectativa entre la hinchada verdolaga, pues representa la posibilidad de presenciar un traspaso de alta categoría que cruzaría el Atlántico sin escalas hacia la Serie A de Italia. Históricamente, Atlético Nacional se ha consolidado como la institución modelo en Colombia en cuanto a la gestión, formación y venta de futbolistas al exterior. Desde las instalaciones de Guarne, el club paisa ha perfeccionado una estructura de divisiones inferiores capaz de abastecer no solo a la Selección Colombia en sus diferentes categorías, sino también de cerrar operaciones récord con clubes de Europa, México y la MLS. Casos recientes de jugadores formados en la casa o potenciados en la institución demuestran que el mercado europeo confía plenamente en el rigor táctico y técnico con el que se trabaja en Medellín. Que el nombre de una nueva 'joya' de la plantilla comience a vincularse con un club de la envergadura del Milan confirma que el proceso formativo goza de excelente salud y mantiene los estándares de exigencia que el mercado internacional demanda. El Milan ha reorientado su estrategia deportiva en los últimos años apostando por una mezcla equilibrada entre experiencia internacional de máxima jerarquía y la frescura de jóvenes promesas globales. La presencia de figuras consagradas como el mediocampista croata Luka Modrić —emblemático cerebro multicampeón que aporta veteranía, liderazgo y una lectura inigualable del juego en el mediocampo rossonero— se ha convertido en el entorno ideal para arropar y acelerar la curva de aprendizaje de Juveniles talentosos. Para un jugador sudamericano que da el salto a la élite europea, coincidir en el vestuario con un ganador del Balón de Oro representa un masterclass diario de profesionalismo. La directiva del cuadro lombardo busca constantemente perlas en el mercado sudamericano con la capacidad técnica para adaptarse rápidamente al ritmo táctico del Calcio, y perfiles dinámicos, con desequilibrio, visión de juego o gran despliegue físico encajan perfectamente en la hoja de ruta del club milanista. Aunque las negociaciones y los sondeos preliminares se manejan con la prudencia característica de las gerencias deportivas, el perfil del canterano de Atlético Nacional seduce por varias razones fundamentales: Versatilidad técnica: Capacidad para asociarse en espacios reducidos, un sello distintivo que se cultiva en la escuela antioqueña. Personalidad competitiva: Acostumbrado desde temprana edad a la presión mediática y la obligación perpetua de ganar que impone Atlético Nacional en cada torneo local. Proyección física y mental: Jugadores jóvenes con la madurez necesaria para asumir el rigor táctico defensivo y ofensivo que exige el fútbol italiano. Adaptarse a la Serie A no es una tarea sencilla debido al rigor defensivo y la velocidad de ejecución, pero contar con padrinos futbolísticos de la talla de Modrić dentro de la plantilla facilita enormemente la transición y aclanta el camino hacia la consolidación estelar. Por ahora, los directivos de Atlético Nacional manejan la situación con cautela institucional, conscientes de que una oferta formal procedente de un gigante europeo de la Serie A pondrá a prueba la solidez financiera y deportiva del club. Los aficionados, por su parte, viven el momento entre el orgullo de ver florecer un talento puramente de la casa y la nostalgia anticipada de saber que las grandes figuras efímeras vuelan temprano hacia los escenarios más exigentes del planeta. El nombre de la joya verdolaga ya está anotado en las agendas de los directores deportivos en Europa. El tiempo dirá si el próximo gran embajador tricolor cruza el charco para estampar su firma y compartir el césped de San Siro con uno de los mejores mediocampistas de la historia del fútbol mundial.

articles.title: Hincha de Boca viajó más de 7.000 kilómetros en su moto de trabajo para la final de Copa Sudamericana
articles.standfirst: De repartidor a la tribuna: recorrió más de 7.000 km en su moto de trabajo para ver a Boca en Barranquilla
articles.summary: De repartidor a la tribuna: recorrió más de 7.000 km en su moto de trabajo para ver a Boca en Barranquilla
articles.body: Hay amores que desafían la lógica, que ignoran los mapas y que reducen cualquier obstáculo financiero a una simple anécdota frente a la inmensidad de una pasión. En el fútbol sudamericano, la devoción por los colores suele traspasar los límites de lo imaginable, pero lo que ha protagonizado Pablo Barrionuevo, un joven hincha de Boca Juniors, entra directamente en la categoría de gesta histórica. A punta de coraje, café, horas de asfalto y sobre su fiel motocicleta de trabajo —una modesta Honda GLH 150—, este repartidor argentino emprendió un viaje colosal de aproximadamente 7.800 kilómetros para llegar hasta Barranquilla, Colombia, donde el próximo 21 de noviembre de 2026 el club de sus amores disputará la gran final de la Copa Sudamericana frente al Atlético Mineiro. Oriundo de El Palomar y radicado en San Miguel, en la provincia de Buenos Aires, Pablo trabajaba habitualmente como delivery. Ante la imposibilidad de costear los elevados precios de los tiquetes aéreos para cruzar el continente, tomó una decisión que dejó perplejos a propios y extraños: en lugar de quedarse lamentándose en casa, decidió subirse a su instrumento diario de subsistencia. "Yo tengo una moto de delivery, yo soy delivery. Yo vine acá a Colombia con mi herramienta de trabajo", relató Pablo con orgullo desde la ruta, consciente de que el esfuerzo físico y mecánico que exigía semejante empresa era monumental. El itinerario no fue improvisado; exigió una planificación milimétrica por el cono sur y la costa del Pacífico. Su ruta inicial abarcó el cruce por provincias argentinas como Santa Fe, Santiago del Estero, Salta y Jujuy, para luego subir hacia Purmamarca y escalar la cordillera por el desafiante Paso de Jama. Desde allí, adentrarse en Chile significó recorrer casi todo su territorio de sur a norte, antes de empalmar con Perú y enfilar directamente hacia Ecuador y Colombia. Los primeros días de travesía avanzaron con cautela, pero con el cronómetro pisándole los talones ante la cercanía de la final en el renovado estadio Metropolitano Roberto Meléndez, Pablo tuvo que acelerar el paso. En los tramos más pesados del trayecto, llegó a devorar hasta 700 kilómetros diarios, soportando el cansancio extremo, las variaciones climáticas de la alta montaña y la soledad de las carreteras secundarias. Sin embargo, a medida que su historia comenzó a viralizarse en redes sociales y a través de medios de comunicación, la travesía se transformó también en una experiencia de hermandad latinoamericana. En cada parada, ciudadanos colombianos y fanáticos de distintos equipos comenzaron a escribirle mensajes de apoyo, ofreciéndole desde palabras de aliento hasta platos de comida caliente, hospedaje y ayuda con combustible. La empatía superó cualquier rivalidad futbolera: el sacrificio de un trabajador argentino removió fibras íntimas en tierras caribeñas, convirtiendo su recorrido en un símbolo de la pasión universal por el deporte. La magnitud de su esfuerzo no tardó en tocar puertas importantes dentro del mundo xeneize. En la recta final de su recorrido, Pablo recibió un contacto clave: un allegado a Leandro Paredes se comunicó con él tras conocer su historia en los medios, prometiéndole una entrada para asegurar su lugar en una de las tribunas del coloso barranquillero. Las horas de frío, polvo y desgaste comenzaban a encontrar su recompensa más preciada. Aun así, una vez que el árbitro pite el final del partido y se conozca la suerte de Boca en la final continental, a Pablo le quedará por resolver un último rompecabezas logístico: el retorno a casa. Como él mismo lo ha advertido, no puede permitirse abandonar su moto en tierras colombianas, ya que de ella depende el sustento diario de su hogar. Pensando en el día después, ya evalúa alternativas para repatriar el vehículo —ya sea en camión o mediante alguna encomienda especial—, priorizando regresar con urgencia a la Argentina tras cumplir su sueño. Mientras Barranquilla se engalana para recibir a miles de hinchas argentinos y brasileños en una fiesta que promete paralizar el continente, la odisea de Pablo Barrionuevo quedará grabada como una de las páginas más pintorescas y conmovedoras de la Copa Sudamericana. Demuestra que, para el hincha sudamericano, las distancias no se miden en kilómetros, sino en latidos; y que cuando se trata de alentar al club de los amores, ningún sacrificio es demasiado grande si al final del camino espera una pelota rodando y el grito sagrado de gol.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham slams angry gamblers who flood her DMs after bets don't hit
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham says thousands of DMs from gamblers blame her for lost bets, and the free agent guard refuses to lose sleep over the angry WNBA bettors.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham is fed up with the gamblers who are blaming her for their losses, which are out of her control in the first place. During the latest episode of "No Hesitation with Sophie Cunningham & Drew Hanlen," the free agent guard revealed she receives "thousands of DMs" from people who say she "didn't do something" during a game which leads to gambling losses. It's a tale as old as time. The psychologists who work with degenerates call this blame-shifting and categorize this as a cognitive distortion. Whatever you want to call it, Sophie's sick of it. JORDAN SPIETH SAYS GAMBLING IS FUELING ROWDY GOLF CROWDS AND WANTS THE SPORT TO ADDRESS IT SOON "I could show you, I'm not even kidding, thousands of DMs of people and like getting mad at me because I didn't do something and they lost a lot of money," Cunningham told Hanlen. "And I'm like, 'Hey, don't be [an] effing idiot. Why would you—like bet on Kelsey [Mitchell] or Caitlyn [Clark] or Aaliyah [Boston]? Why are you betting on me? Like, I don't even know what's going to happen that game. Like, I don't have the control. I don't have the ball enough to know if I'm going to get one three-point shot or if I'm going to get 10 of them." While Cunningham has to deal with the degenerates blaming her, the WNBA is in bed with gambling markets. FanDuel and DraftKings are primary sponsors of the league. When it comes to betting and gambling, since all that has like really happened and it's really come into our league as well, fans are so much more vocal about when you don't perform," Cunningham added. articles.title: Dejounte Murray Was Upset When the Pelicans Drafted Jeremiah Fears
articles.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans continue to be a mess, and Dejounte Murray’s name keeps making the headlines in the midst of it all. It was recently reported that h...
articles.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans continue to be a mess, and Dejounte Murray's name keeps making the headlines in the midst of it all. It was recently reported that he wants to be traded from the Pelicans, after cryptic social media posts pointed towards his growing discontent.

But if the Pelicans want to move the disgruntled guard, it's going to come at a price for New Orleans. It will likely cost at least one first-round pick for the Pelicans to move off Murray. That's not surprising, given he's played just 45 games over the last two seasons.

There's quite a bit of news surrounding Murray, but the latest tidbit centers on the Pelicans' 2025 draft selections. Murray was "upset" that the Pelicans drafted guard Jeremiah Fears, according to Yahoo Sports' Kelly Iko.

Murray upset that the Pelicans drafted Fears

Fears, who just became the youngest player in Pelicans history to record a triple-double in a win that ended the team's six-game losing streak, has been impressive to start the season. He's averaging career highs, is shooting the ball more efficiently than a year ago and looks to be a building block for New Orleans' future.

Murray, meanwhile, has become a negative asset for the Pelicans. A high-ranking executive said, "No one wants to touch him," per Iko, in regards to Murray.

With Fears, Zion Williamson and Derik Queen, the Pelicans might actually have a nucleus to build around, but there's several ill-fitting players on the roster, Murray included, who are causing more harm than good for the team. Williamson has already called out the team for lack of effort after an embarrassing loss to the Nets last week, and Murray's displeasure only amplifies the issues in New Orleans.

Not the first time Murray's been upset by a franchise's decisions

Murray has undeniable talent as a versatile two-way guard, someone who earned an All-Star selection and All-Defensive honors. He's also someone who has exited teams on bad terms in the past, specifically with San Antonio. Murray has spoken openly on the "All the Smoke" podcast with Stephen Jackson and Matt Barnes about how he felt the Spurs were playing "mind games" with him early in his career and wanted to be traded elsewhere due to a lack of playing time.

"They playing other guys that was second round picks, undrafted in front of me," Murray said. "Now I'm just like, what's going on? I'm hitting Rich [Paul]. I'm like, 'I gotta get traded.' He's like, 'You ain't got no value.' I'm like, this is too much. What did they put me through, I don't understand."

Murray took aim at Hall of Famer Tony Parker specifically, who was on the team in Murray's rookie year. Murray said Parker didn't have interest in mentoring him, which he said led to Parker being traded to the Charlotte Hornets.

"I know he didn't like it, because if he liked it, he would have mentored me the way he should have," Murray said. "He wouldn't have went to Charlotte. He would have stayed right there."

After five years in San Antonio, Murray was eventually traded to the Atlanta Hawks, but his final season with the Spurs was the best of his career.

articles.title: McLaren And Toyota Push GT3 Development Hard For 2027
articles.summary: McLaren and Toyota race to finish their new hypercars. Both teams share testing secrets and tight deadlines before the 2027 season starts.
articles.body:
McLaren and Toyota are not waiting around. Both makers are rushing to get their new race cars ready for the 2027 season. They are using every day to fix small issues before the big races start. This push shows they know the clock is ticking loud.

McLaren is moving into a new stage of its plan. The team boss James Barclay says the group is finally ready to test with all six drivers at once. This step was the main goal after they picked their full lineup. "That's going to be a great opportunity to get the group together," Barclay told reporters during the recent 6 Hours of Monza. The team plans two more tests before the year ends. One of these runs will happen at Portimao later this month. They want to make sure the car works well before they build more parts.

McLaren used just one car for all its tests so far. This choice helped them focus on fixing parts before they made copies. They want to be sure everything is right before they commit to two cars. "We started early for that reason," Barclay said. If they started later, they would have to work twice as hard to catch up. The team is still watching the world situation to see if they need to change their test locations. But the plan is set for now.

Toyota also had a big week with its new GR GT3. The car made its first race appearance at Motegi in Japan. It did not score points because it was not fully approved yet. But the team saw what it needed to see. "The main purpose was to discover any issues on the car," Masaya Kaji told Sportscar365 . They found a sensor problem that hurt their top speed.

The team chose Motegi because they could test tires right after the race. This saved them time and helped them learn fast. Kaji noted that the car performed well despite the issues. "Of course we were not trying to be so quick, because there was a championship battle going on, but the performance level was ok." Toyota wants to get official approval soon. They hope to race at the test in Daytona on Dec. 10-11.

The next step for both teams is clear. They must finish their work before the season starts. Kaji said the approval process is moving along. "It looks ok, and hopefully we can get it in the very near future." He added that the wait will not last long. "I don't know exactly when, but it's not so far away." Toyota expects the car to run in many races next year.

articles.title: Former Michigan WR Semaj Morgan takes shot at Big House crowd
articles.summary: Morgan reflects on returning to a former team where he won a championship while focusing on the current process.
articles.body:
In Ann Arbor, wide receiver Semaj Morgan had some highs and he had some lows. His punt return against Iowa in the 2023 Big Ten Championship Game and his touchdown against Texas in 2024 are among the highs. But numerous drops and struggles in the return game were among the lows.

However, after a change of scenery to UCLA , Morgan is a man renewed, posting career highs with 41 catches for 525 yards and three touchdowns -- more than double any of his receiving yards any given season with Michigan football. His 525 yards would be second on this current Wolverines team, behind only JJ Buchanan, the star receiver who is out for the season now.

Morgan is excited to return to The Big House with his undefeated Bruins , but he's also not trying to put too much on his return to the stadium he spent three years playing in.

"Definitely, but the process is a process, and we got to keep going what we did to come this far," Morgan said. "We don't want to change the process based on our opponent. But it is kind of a special thing for me. I spent some time there, won a championship there, so it is going to be nice going back there. But I don't want to overthink about it. I just want to keep the process."

Morgan has always been outspoken, if not blunt. When he shared his message to his UCLA teammates about what to expect about the environment at Michigan Stadium, he did not mince words.

"Oh, yeah, I told them what it's like," Morgan said. "It's a nice big stadium, older fans, so it's not that loud, so we're gonna have fun."

That might hold a kernel of truth, but given that UCLA struggles to even get the Rose Bowl to half full, it's not quite the dig that it could have otherwise been.

Michigan and UCLA will kick off at 3:30 p.m. EST at The Big House, with the game set to be televised on CBS.

articles.title: Dan Campbell won't wallow in "what ifs" arising from injuries
articles.summary: The Lions have, in recent weeks, lost both linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (knee) to significant injuries.
articles.body:
The Lions have, in recent weeks, lost both linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (knee) to significant injuries. Coach Dan Campbell won't wallow in worrying about what may have been if the injuries hadn't occurred.

"I think there's times where, if you're not careful, you lay in bed at night and you start thinking about all the 'what ifs,'" Campbell told reporters on Tuesday. "And at some point, you just become a miserable piece of shit. And I'm not gonna do it, man. We're not doing it.

"I refuse to look at it that way. Does it sting? Yeah, it sure did in the moment. It's time to move on. We have to.

"And what has happened with Jack Campbell and with Hutch now will not be in vain. We can't allow it to. They got us to this point. And so what are we gonna do about it, man? Are we just gonna let it go to waste, or are we gonna do something and pick up the slack?"

It's the right attitude. Injuries happen. Sometimes, they happen to great players. (The more great players a team has, the greater the chances that one of them will be injured.)

The only approach is to tap the next man up on the shoulder, expect him to do his job to the best of his ability, not allow it to become a "woe is us" situation, and keep going.

That becomes easier, of course, if a team has quality depth. Which is why some teams that are top heavy with highly-paid stars find themselves in a pinch when those stars aren't available to play.

articles.title: Dolphins place defensive linemen Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips on injured reserve
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins placed defensive linemen Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips on injured reserve Tuesday, a significant blow for a defense that will now be wi...
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins placed defensive linemen Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips on injured reserve Tuesday, a significant blow for a defense that will now be without its top three linemen for an extended period.

The Dolphins already lost veteran Zach Sieler last week to a season-ending ruptured biceps . Biggers suffered a knee injury in the second quarter of Miami's Week 10 loss at Indianapolis, and Phillips left that game with an upper-body injury in the fourth.

Coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that Biggers and Phillips were set to undergo testing on the severity of the injuries, adding that he had "concerns."

Both players were expected to see increased roles in Sieler's absence.

Phillips had been one of Miami's best players against the run, recording 28 tackles and a tackle for loss while making many more impact plays that Hafley said wouldn't show up on the stat sheet. Biggers has 18 tackles and a sack this season.

To fill their roster spots, the Dolphins signed quarterback Brady Cook, defensive lineman Jordan Jefferson and edge Eric Watts to the active roster off the practice squad. Cook will back up interim starter Kyle McCord .

Miami also added several players to the practice squad, including receiver Brady Boyd, defensive linemen Chris Smith and Matthew Butler and kicker Daniel Carlson.

The Dolphins brought in Carlson to replace Zane Gonzalez, who was waived Monday after missing three kicks against the Colts.

articles.title: Deion Sanders’ GF Karrueche Tran Makes Candid Admission on Handling Mood Shifts with Prime After Colorado Losses: “Don’t Try to Talk”
articles.summary: Colorado’s losing streaks have made life increasingly difficult for Deion Sanders. Four years into his tenure in Boulder, Coach Prime is still searching for...
articles.body:
Colorado's losing streaks have made life increasingly difficult for Deion Sanders. Four years into his tenure in Boulder, Coach Prime is still searching for the consistency that could turn the Buffaloes into contenders. And while the pressure is obvious on the football field, what happens after the final whistle is another story. His girlfriend Karrueche Tran has now revealed what the mood at home looks like after a loss.

During her appearance on The Pop Exchange Show , Jason Kennedy put Tran on the spot with an interesting question: what's the mood like at home after a tough loss? Tran didn't hold back as she revealed how she handles those difficult moments, while Sanders, apparently, tends to retreat into his gloomy mood.

"There's definitely a mood and energy shift from losing and winning a game," she admitted. "Losing is like it's just hard because the team, everybody's they're down, and they're thinking about the game, and it's like what can you really say to make them feel better outside."

In her answer, Tran revealed that she understands how gloomy the mood at home can get after a loss. That's why she tries to divert Coach Prime's mind from the game and refrains from talking about football.

"I can follow the game, but I don't know all the technical, like, 'Oh, the offense did this,' and then, I don't, that's not my thing, and he knows that," said Tran.

"So, I'll say my piece of, like, 'I'm sorry or whatever.' And I just nurture him or take care of him in any other way. But I don't try to talk football because then he's just going to be like, 'What are you, what are you talking about?'"

Fans are well aware of how restless Sanders can become following a defeat. Back in 2023, the Buffaloes suffered a heartbreaking 43-46 loss to Stanford, a massive shock to the team.

Colorado had entered halftime with a commanding 29-0 lead, only to watch it slip away. The defeat clearly got to Sanders. In the days that followed, he spent hours at Folsom Field, analysing every aspect of the game, unable to put the loss behind him.

"It's tough. I stayed in the stadium for a couple days. That was the one almighty. I had never been in that situation before in my life. That was a little tough," Sanders told the reporters after the game.

"I'm a 'why' guy. I've got to find out the 'why' of everything in life. Why are you playing football? Why did you do this? And I analyze this stuff. When I'm home, even resting, I'm exhausting my mind. It's one thing to sleep and get rest, but if you don't turn off, it's hard for me to turn off my mind. So if I don't turn off my mind, I don't get rest. You get sleep, but you don't get rest."

That's not all. The same thing happened last year when the Buffaloes suffered another humiliating defeat, falling 53-7 to Utah. It was one of the heaviest losses of Sanders' head-coaching career, rivalled only by the 56-14 defeat to Washington State.

The loss clearly took a toll on Sanders, so much so that he admitted during a press briefing, "I haven't been home yet. I've been here every night since. I haven't been home yet."

Losing is never easy, and for a man like Sanders, winning is simply non-negotiable. However, his recent struggles with the Colorado Buffaloes suggest otherwise. And if this losing trend continues, Tran might find herself having to steer the conversation away from football every single week.

articles.title: Despite specter of ICE looming, fans welcome Haiti-US match in Cincinnati
articles.summary: As Haiti and the United States national soccer teams prepare to take the field for the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League match-up on Nov.17, the st...
articles.body:
As Haiti and the United States national soccer teams prepare to take the field for the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League match-up on Nov.17, the stadium they will play in sits just 16 miles from an Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) office.

For many fans of Haiti in the region, the game at TQL Stadium is an opportunity to celebrate national pride despite a bruising loss to the U.S. in Miami Saturday. For others, the excitement comes with heightened concern about immigration agents, whose actions in carrying out the administration's mass deportation agenda have caused widespread panic and humiliation for Haitians in Ohio.

"There's a lot of things that are going on right now that are unfortunate, so it's nice to come together and actually be happy about something," said Asecou Clermon, who plans to attend the match.

"Whether we win or lose, it will be just a good environment to be in," Clermon added.

ICE's offices in suburban Blue Ash are a 25-minute drive from TQL Stadium. Over the summer, after the Trump administration ended TPS for Haiti, the site became a well-known location to the estimated 20,000 Haitian newcomers in the region. Many living in Springfield, long a target of President Donald Trump , and elsewhere were summoned to the Blue Ash offices for check-ins.

By August, videos of Haitians being fitted with GPS ankle monitors went viral as ICE arrests increased overall around the region. Advocates also rallied outside the offices to protest detentions there.

For Haitian immigrants living in the region, even those with legal status, the office became a source of anxiety where they or family members and friends have faced deportation. It also drew attention after Pierre Damas Bel died by suicide for being the location where the 20-year-old traveled to request that his ankle monitor be removed.

Overall, the ICE office's proximity to the stadium illustrates a contrasting experience for the Haitian community in many ways. At one location, Haitians face immigration procedures that have placed their futures in the balance. At the other, the USMNT is welcoming their country's athletes as sports guests.

Chris Knoester, a sport sociologist at The Ohio State University who has led the National Sports and Society Survey (NSASS) , said the Haiti-US match carries significance beyond athletic competition.

"Sports interactions can be symbolic, influential, and meaningful on many different levels," Knoester said. "They are never just a form of entertainment or display of athleticism."

"Especially in the wake of outrageous lies, scapegoating, and targeted immigration enforcement aimed at Haitian Americans, the upcoming Haiti-USA match is likely to carry extraordinary significance," Knoester explained.

On Match day, however, questions for policymakers, community organizations, and institutions will take a backseat as Haiti fans put their primary objective front and center.

For Haitian immigrants in Ohio, the opportunity to see their national team compete on American soil may offer a rare moment of connection and joy amid difficult circumstances. In addition to immigration policies that caused many to avoid outings or reduce their incomes this year, some Haitians in the Midwest found the matches featuring Haiti during the 2026 FIFA World Cup either too expensive or too far to attend in Boston, Philadelphia and Atlanta.

Tuesday's game is within driving distance not only for central Ohio Haitians, but also for those living in nearby Indiana and other Midwestern cities. Ticket prices were as low as $40 the day before the match, a much more affordable option than the Miami leg, where prices exceeded $150.

Party promoters have also used Tuesday's game to organize several after-parties as an option to celebrate outside the stadium.

Natafon Korel says he has to support, even though immigration enforcement affecting Haitians in the area have left him "more aware and more alarmed."

"I do want to be more aware of, you know, watching my surroundings," Korel said. "Just having that culture around me is another thing that drove me to go."

For Smith Francois, a local activist, the trip to Cincinnati will mark his first time ever attending a professional soccer game. He plans to go with other Haitian fans, drawn by the opportunity to share in the occasion.

"To celebrate this moment," Francois said.

This report is a collaboration between The Haitian Times and The Associated Press.

articles.title: Dallas’ Week 10 loss is that it’s more than just “the little things”
articles.summary: A coaching mismatch, poor run defense, and the importance of the pass rush are things Dallas learned from their Week 10 loss to the 49ers
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys had a chance to flip their season around and vanquish a boogieman all in one home effort , but they couldn't outscore the San Francisco 49ers. The New York Giants ' loss on Thursday opened the door for the Cowboys, but Kyle Shanahan, Deebo Samuel, and Christian McCaffrey slammed it in their face. Brian Schottenheimer, who said, "The fight on the team was right, but it was the little things that are killing them," fell to 0-9-1 against non-NFC teams not in his division. Looking at the stats, "the little things" could mean the difference in coaching ability.

The coaching mismatch was obvious. The Dallas defense was atrocious, and the offense got started a touch too late to overcome a 38-19 deficit in the fourth quarter. San Francisco broke the record for most yards gained against a Cowboys defense at AT&T Stadium, with 584 yards even though Mike Evans was out, Deebo Samuel just returning from injury, and Keenan Allen just got to the locker room this week. The 49ers ran the ball for over 200 yards, and Brock Purdy threw for 389 yards and three touchdowns.

The main thing Dallas might need to learn is the coaching difference was the most significant issue for Dallas.

Shanahan showed his coaching advantage in the second half

The teams were nearly identical at the half. The Cowboys' kicker, Brandon Aubrey, missed an extra point, putting them behind by a single point, 17-16. The 49ers' made their adjustments at the break and came out with an excellent plan of attack, scoring touchdowns on three straight drives.

The first went 81 yards in five plays, the second took only three plays to go 80, and the final drive was 12 plays, 90 yards, and over seven minutes. In contrast, Dallas drove for a 52-yard field goal and threw an interception before falling 38-19 in the fourth quarter. The first three drives of the second half, accumulating 251 yards and 21 points was a masterclass from an elite playcaller.

As good as some like Quinnen Williams and Otitto Ogbonnia have played lately, the overall run defense has still been among the worst in the NFL. Only the Las Vegas Raiders are worse. Going into Week 10, Dallas allowed just under 150 rushing yards per game and 5 yards per attempt, with 11 touchdowns allowed. The 49ers ran for 7.4 yards per carry, totaling 214 yards and three scores. They had Samuel running for over 25 yards per rush, and Brock Purdy scrambled for over 10.5 yards per carry. McCaffrey and Kaelon Black both went for 4.8 per attempt.

The 49ers were more physical, especially on Black's rush attempts, and their change-of-direction runs had the entire Cowboys' defense fooled. The team might be last against the run after Week 10.

The pass rush changes the ability of the defense

It wasn't a lockdown performance, but holding the 49ers offense to under 200 yards and 20 points in the first half looks incredible compared to the 250 yards and 28 points from the second half. If Dallas only allowed 34 points they might have upset San Francisco.

The most significant difference for the Cowboys was the pressure they got on Purdy. James Houston and Ogbonnia shared the game's first sack, with Williams adding a team-leading sixth sack on the same drive. Newly returned Jonathan Bullard added another first-half sack, and rookie LT Overton took down Purdy for the final one of the half.

That was a season high for Dallas in sacks in a half. In the second half, the pass rush was eliminated by San Francisco. Elijah Garcia got the only second-half sack on the first play of the fourth quarter, and the defense wasn't the same. The Cowboys can't leave their injured defensive backs to cover as long as they did in the second half versus the 49ers, or they could lose to anyone. The team has to carry that first have performance forward and continue it throughout the entire game.

articles.title: Mason McTavish Seeks Revenge As Blues Face Ducks Tuesday
articles.summary: Mason McTavish returns to Anaheim with a chip on his shoulder. Two Blues X-factors could decide Tuesday night's game against a surging Ducks squad.
articles.body:
The St. Louis Blues host a very young and fast Anaheim squad on Tuesday night. The Blues need a win after getting throttled by Florida, 4-1, in their last outing. Mason McTavish returns to face his former team with a clear motive for revenge. Things ended on a muddy note for McTavish and the Ducks, leaving him with feelings to settle. Bleedin Blue reports No. 83 has seven goals this season and might become the second Blues player to reach double digits alongside Jimmy Snuggerud.

Jimmy Snuggerud has transformed into the scoring engine the Blues need to win hockey games. He continues to excel in every opportunity thrown his way while pulling away from Dalibor Dvorsky. Snuggerud is handling the scoring role well and keeps the team in the hunt. A hat-trick against McTavish's old team would be a perfect way to reach ten goals. The Ducks counter with Cutter Gauthier, who leads the charge with an astounding 14 goals this month. Per Bleedin Blue, Gauthier has 14 goals in November and could chase the NHL record of 20 set by Joe Malone and Teemu Selanne. He has seven more games to play in November to make that history happen.

Goaltender Joel Hofer is expected to start after the team got a break following the loss to Florida. Following that poor defeat, he must recover quickly to halt the negative momentum. A flawless 5-0 mark versus the Ducks belongs to Hofer, who maintains a Goals Against Average of 1.38. Bleedin Blue states he surrendered merely eight goals across more than 347 minutes played against Anaheim. All it takes is one win for Hofer to start building a case for Vezina Trophy votes.

articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Schedule, results & prize money
articles.summary: Everything you need to know about the 2026 Grand Slam of Darts as world number one Luke Littler targets a third straight success in Wolverhampton.
articles.body:
The 2026 Grand Slam of Darts is under way and another of the Professional Darts Corporation's (PDC) major titles is set to be won in Wolverhampton.

This edition is bigger than ever, with 48 players taking part, and unlike most of darts' major tournaments, the players are split into groups in the initial phase, rather than a straight knockout format.

Each player will face two opponents in their group, with only the group winner progressing into the last 16.

The rest of the competition is a straight knockout format.

Luke Littler is the defending champion following a 16-11 victory over Luke Humphries in the 2025 final to become world number one for the first time.

Littler faces a tough start, with Beau Greaves his opponent on the opening evening, and Neils Zonneveld, who beat Littler in their only previous meeting, completing the group.

The tournament lasts for nine days from Saturday, 14 November to Sunday, 22 November.

Group stage (14-17 November) - 48 matches

Second round (18-19 November) - eight matches

In the group stage, the format is best of nine legs, or first to five legs.

In the initial phase, two points are awarded for a win, with the group winner progressing to the last 16. In case of players being level on points at the end of the group phase, the following tie-breakers apply:

Highest Total Tournament Average (to two decimal places)

Highest Winning Match Average (to two decimal places)

Second-round matches are a best-of-19 format, or first to 10 legs.

The quarter-finals, semi-finals and final are best of 31 legs, or first to 16 legs.

Who is playing and how did they qualify?

With the tournament expanded, a new set of qualification rules have been put in place.

Up to 24 players could qualify from reaching a major PDC televised final in the past 12 months, but only nine ended up qualifying via that route, partly because of the dominance Littler has shown.

Ten players reached Wolverhampton from the PDC youth, development and challenge tours, the Women's Matchplay and Women's Series and championships from across the globe.

Six more secured places through the European Tour, while 13 qualified with a Players Championship win.

The final 10 spots, which include ninth seed Stephen Bunting, were claimed in a PDC tour card holder qualifying event.

From there, the top-16 ranked players in the PDC's order of merit were seeded and filled pot one. The next 16 went into pot two and the final 16 made up pot three. One player from each pot was then allocated to a group.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland seal second with win over 10-man Kosovo
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland secure second spot in Group B3 with a 3-0 victory over 10-man Kosovo in their final Nations League game at the Aviva Stadium.
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland secured second spot in Group B3 with a comfortable 3-0 victory over 10-man Kosovo in their final Nations League game at the Aviva Stadium.

Troy Parrott continued his fine scoring form for the Irish with two confidently taken penalties while Jack Moylan also got on the scoresheet.

Parrott tucked away the first on 28 minutes after Kreshnik Hajrizi was sent off for handling his initial effort on the line.

He fired home the second three minutes after the restart after he was fouled in the box, before the impressive Moylan then glanced home a third on 75 minutes.

The second-place finish confirms Republic of Ireland's place in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw next month and also ensures they have a promotion/relegation play-off against a League A team as they try to move up to the top tier for the first time.

Kosovo, who won 1-0 when the two sides met in September, made a confident start in Dublin and were inches away from taking the lead on 17 minutes.

Fisnik Asllani got in behind on the right and cut the ball back to Lindon Emerllahu, whose low effort flashed just wide.

They went close again when a volley from captain Vedat Muriqi was smothered by Caoimhin Kelleher.

Momentum swung firmly in Republic of Ireland's favour on 26 minutes as Hajrizi stopped Parrott's goal-bound header on the line with his hand.

That resulted in a red card for the defender and a penalty, which Parrott slammed home into the top corner.

The Real Betis striker spurned a chance to double their advantage soon after as he glanced wide from Ryan Manning's pinpoint cross before Jayson Molumby forced a low save from Arijanet Muric.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side raced out of the blocks in the second half and almost found a second a minute in when James Abankwah met substitute Harvey Vale's cross with a volley, which was palmed away by Muric.

From the resulting corner Dara O'Shea, on his 50th cap, headed over before Republic of Ireland won another penalty on 48 minutes.

Molumby's fierce strike was pushed out by Muric, who then clipped Parrott as the forward raced in to get to the rebound.

The 24-year-old stepped up again and fired the ball straight down the middle for his 12th goal in his last nine competitive games for his country.

The Irish continued to pile forward and were rewarded for persistent pressure with a third on 75 minutes as Moylan headed home from an inviting cross from substitute Liam Kitching.

Republic of Ireland analysis: Parrott delivers again as Irish end campaign on a high

After pushing Austria close on Saturday before ultimately falling to a 1-0 defeat, Hallgrimsson wanted his side to "mirror" that performance against Kosovo, confident that it would ensure they got the desired outcome of a home win and he was proved right.

Like in Austria, the Irish struggled to get going early on, but the red card and awarding of the penalty changed the game.

Parrott, as he has done for the past year in a green shirt, delivered with two more goals at the Aviva, both from the penalty spot, to give Hallgrimsson's side a platform to build upon.

He won both penalties and kept his cool to convert both to continue his fine scoring run for his country and shrug off his recent struggles at club level.

Republic of Ireland's passivity was noticeable in their off day in Pristina two months ago, but there was more bite and urgency from them in Dublin, particularly in their fast start to the second half.

Moylan scored his fifth international goal and produced another impressive display as he grows in stature on this stage, while they managed to keep Muriqi, who scored the winner in September's meeting, quiet as they kept a clean sheet for only the second time in this campaign.

A year and a day on from taking second place in World Cup qualifying with a famous late 3-2 win over Hungary, Republic of Ireland have concluded their Nations League campaign with the second-place finish they set out to achieve and with Parrott at the heart of it again.

It was not anywhere near as dramatic or emotive as that famous night in Budapest, but, like that win, it is another important result as it gets them pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw.

Before attention turns to that campaign, the next step for Hallgrimsson's team will be to earn promotion to League A by winning March's play-off, which they will have to do without Liam Scales and Ryan Manning, who both were booked on Tuesday.

It will be a tough ask, but one the Irish should relish as they will always be a threat with the in-form Parrott in their ranks.

articles.title: Three NASCAR Playoff Drivers Facing A Tough 2027 Return
articles.summary: Ryan Preece, Chris Buescher, and Daniel Suarez made the 2026 playoffs, but changes at their teams and the series suggest a hard road back in 2027.
articles.body:
The NASCAR Cup Series postseason field changes every single year. The 16 drivers who qualified in 2026 will not all be back in 2027. Three specific drivers face an uphill climb to make the cut again. Ryan Preece, Chris Buescher, and Daniel Suarez are the names to watch. Their paths to next year's playoffs look much harder than the path they took this year.

Ryan Preece made the 2026 playoffs by avoiding crashes, not by winning races. He finished in the top 20 often enough to qualify. Before his win at Daytona, he had not finished higher than eighth all year. He did not finish a single race higher than 10th during the playoffs. This lack of speed is a big problem now that Brad Keselowski is gone from RFK Racing. Preece moved from the No. 60 car to the No. 6 Ford for 2027. The No. 60 car will not have a charter next year. That leaves the team with less stability. Preece proved you can make the playoffs by just staying on track. He might find that trick does not work when the competition gets tougher.

Chris Buescher qualified for the 2026 playoffs because the rules changed. The old "win and in" rule was gone. He finished 10th in the regular season standings. But once the playoffs started, he struggled mightily. He fell from 10th in points to finish 16th, last among all playoff drivers. His only top 10 finish since mid-July was at Charlotte Motor Speedway. Roush Fenway Racing remained the team name in 2020 and 2021, yet he failed to qualify for the playoffs. He won five races from 2022 to 2024 with Keselowski as a co-owner. Now that Keselowski has left, the team dynamic has shifted again. Buescher might not have the same safety net in the points standings next year.

Daniel Suarez faces a different kind of trouble at Spire Motorsports. Spire is implementing changes as well, though Kaulig Racing stands alone as the only team operating Dodges in 2027. After a lengthy absence, the brand is coming back and must construct a competitive program from scratch. This requires more than just driving speed. A thorough grasp of the car's mechanical operation is required. Kaulig Racing CEO Chris Rice praised a new hire for the job. Rice said, "Aaron has the exact engineering mindset and practical background we need as we lay the groundwork for 2027," according to Yahoo Sports . Because the program begins with no history, the pressure is intense. There are no past setups or data to rely on. Engineers must design every component of the car specifically for this manufacturer. Suarez will have to learn a new machine while trying to beat the best drivers in the field.

No Cup Series season has featured 37 full-time cars since 2021.

articles.title: Bednar, Jeffers accept $23.15 million qualifying offers, records for average salaries at positions
articles.summary: Eight free agents were given the offers by their former teams on November 2nd.
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Yankees closer David Bednar and Minnesota catcher Ryan Jeffers were the only players to accept $23.15 million qualifying offers from their former teams by Tuesday's deadline, both setting records for average annual values at their positions.

Eight free agents were given the offers by their former teams on Nov. 2. Those not accepting included Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki, Seattle outfielder Randy Arozarena, Baltimore left-hander Trevor Rogers, Pittsburgh second baseman Brandon Lowe and San Diego left-hander Adrian Morejon.

First baseman/outfielder Jake Bauers, who received a qualifying offer from Milwaukee, finalized a $58 million, four-year contract with Boston on Tuesday. He gets $16 million in each of the first two seasons, $15 million in 2029 and $11 million in 2030. Bauers would receive a $2 million assignment bonus each time he is traded.

Bednar, a two-time All-Star, was 7-3 with a 2.47 ERA and 35 saves in 39 chances. The salary of the 32-year-old right-hander set a mark for relief pitchers, topping the $23 million averaged by Edwin Díaz in a $69 million, three-year deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers that began this year.

Jeffers set a record for average annual value in a contract for a catcher, surpassing J.T. Realmuto's $23.1 million in a $115.5 million, five-year contract with Philadelphia for 2021-25 . Jeffers, 29, hit .256 with 14 homers and 56 RBIs over 92 games. He was sidelined from the Twins between May 18 and July 10 after breaking his left hamate bone while swinging at a pitch from Houston's AJ Blubaugh that resulted in a foul ball.

Qualifying offers began after the 2012 season and only 20 of 165 prior offers have been accepted. This year's figure is determined by the average of the top 125 major league contracts in 2026.

A free agent can be made a qualifying offer only if he had been with the same team continuously since opening day and had never received a qualifying offer before.

If a team makes a qualifying offer to a player who signs a major league contract with another club before the next amateur draft, his former club receives draft pick compensation at the end of the first round or at the end of competitive balance round B. The placement depends on the amount of the new contract and the revenue-sharing and luxury tax status of the team losing the player.

articles.title: How Jasen Lopez became a 'spark' for FSU football
articles.summary: Amid injuries and coaching changes, freshman Jasen Lopez has become a vital playmaker for Florida State football.
articles.body:
Jasen Lopez has emerged as one of Florida State football's primary threats as a laundry list of injuries has mounted on the Seminoles with two regular-season games left, both at Doak Campbell Stadium .

With Duce Robinson out for the year with a torn ACL and a running back room down to fifth-string Zay Parks as the lone healthy player, more was asked of Lopez and the wide receiver room.

The highly touted freshman had primarily served as the punt returner in the opening half of the season, and only recorded 17 receiving yards on three catches in the first six games. It wasn't until the South Florida native took the field against No. 7 Miami that Lopez finally broke through.

He hauled in one catch, but it was a significant one that picked up 39 yards. Lopez parlayed that into a three-game stretch where he's caught 13 passes for 178 yards in what could only be described as a turbulent month for the Seminoles (5-5, 3-4 ACC) program.

"I mean, there's been a lot of adversity throughout the season. There's been a lot of ups, a lot of downs. But the coaches always preach to us, we got to come in with the same mentality. You know what I'm saying? Just go in there, work hard, do what we can control," Lopez said after practice on Tuesday, Nov. 17. "For me, I've just been staying ready. Trying to take advantage of every opportunity I get. That's my mindset on it. Every opportunity, I'm going to try to capitalize off of it."

See the best moments from FSU football's road trip to Pitt

Lopez was a quality signing for former head coach Mike Norvell. His recruitment was aided by the FSU basketball staff and Luke Loucks, who will add Lopez to his rotation after the football season concludes. Despite heaps of pre-season praise from Norvell, Lopez had limited touches in the opening months of the season, but broke out in what proved to be Norvell's final two games, against Miami and Clemson.

He hauled in four catches for 52 yards and his first collegiate touchdown against the Tigers, a bright spot in a loss that eventually cost Norvell his job . Despite the turbulence, Lopez remained steady and followed up his game against Clemson with 54 yards on four catches. However, his biggest play of the game was a 40-yard punt return that led to the Seminoles' first touchdown in an eventual 31-24 win.

Special teams is an area of pride for Lopez, and he said his experience as a punt returner this season helped him feel ready for his increased role in the offense.

"I would just say it built more confidence for me being more involved in the offense. It just helped me flow. At punt returner, I was thinking with the same mentality, 'If I'm able to get this return, I'm going to try to get the biggest return we could get," Lopez said. "As I've gotten more involved in the offense, it's built more confidence within me."

Lopez has recorded 162 punt return yards on 16 attempts this season. It's an area of his game that he excels in, and one that he works on consistently. But the freshman said the area he's grown most is his speed.

He feels quicker than when he arrived on campus, and he credits that to his work in the weight room and the hours he spent on the practice field working on his releases and reading of defenders. As Lopez continues to grow in his role, he's already finding ways to impact games, and he's becoming a contested-catch specialist with impressive grabs in tight coverage.

In the 16-10 win against Pitt, offensive production was at a premium for everyone but Lopez. He recorded 72 yards on four catches, including a 46-yard grab where he fought off tight coverage from the Panthers' defensive back to spring a much-needed explosive play for the Seminoles offense.

"It's just work that I've put in throughout the years. Working different releases, being able to track the ball. But it comes in early on in the game, you know, seeing different ways they [opponents] play and stuff like that," Lopez said about how he wins 50/50's. "Throughout the game, I'll set him [opposing DB] up one way and see how he moves, and then the next time I'll do it the different way and see how he reacts. That's how I set it up to end up slipping him."

Lopez will continue to be a focal point for the offense, and with two games left in his debut campaign, he said he's grateful to contribute on the field.

"I'm blessed to be able to have that position and impact the game in different ways and build sparks for the team that could help get us going," Lopez said.

articles.title: Jesse Minter says Ravens have two games before bye to stay alive
articles.summary: Jesse Minter says the Ravens have a two-game stretch before their bye to stay alive, putting added urgency on Baltimore's next two contests.
articles.body:
Jesse Minter isn't hiding from the reality of the Baltimore Ravens ' situation. The losing streak continues. The first-year head coach is facing a difficult stretch where his team's remaining postseason hopes hang by a thread. Fate could be determined by how his squad responds over the next two weeks. The standings are becoming increasingly unforgiving, and Baltimore has little room left to recover from another setback.

The Ravens have two games remaining before their bye week, giving them a brief window to change the conversation surrounding the organization. Minter spoke with the media after Monday night's loss to the Los Angeles Chargers . His assessment suggested those games will carry significance beyond the immediate playoff picture.

The message was direct. Baltimore has two games to stay alive, and in the meantime, everything is being evaluated. When asked about the message to a team that had just lost to a winless opponent, Minter didn't offer a vague reminder to keep fighting. Instead, he put a clear timeline on Baltimore's opportunity to remain in the postseason picture.

Jesse Minter says Ravens have two-game stretch to stay alive

Asked about the challenge of getting his team back on track after another loss, Minter offered a revealing assessment of where things stand in Baltimore.

"We have a two-game stretch before our bye to stay alive. That's really where it's at, from a numbers standpoint [and] from a postseason standpoint, and then also just [that] you're evaluating everything... That's just the nature of this game, and so that's where we're at."

That second part carries weight considering the losing streak. Baltimore's problems have extended across the roster, from an offense struggling to establish a reliable running game to a defense that hasn't consistently delivered the performances expected of it. Minter has acknowledged that the team's identity and execution haven't been good enough, and the upcoming stretch gives the Ravens little time to demonstrate otherwise.

The immediate challenge begins against the Carolina Panthers , but the importance of the next two games goes beyond the opponent on the schedule. Baltimore needs to show that it can play complementary football, eliminate turnovers and produce the kind of consistent performance that has been missing during its losing streak.

Minter also made it clear that accountability isn't limited to the players. He has repeatedly acknowledged his own responsibility for the team's shortcomings, including the failure to establish the physical identity the organization wants to represent.

Winning both games would bring Baltimore back to .500 entering the bye. Splitting them would leave the Ravens at 5-7, while two more losses would deepen an already difficult climb. Minter's message reflects that urgency, but his team first has to address the line-of-scrimmage failures that kept it from beating a previously winless opponent.

articles.title: Winter sports season starts with big-time performances on the court
articles.summary: The high school basketball season officially started Monday. And what a start, with impressive individual efforts and big wins for local teams.
articles.body:
Highlights from Monday, Nov. 16, in high school sports:

Sarah Cosio started her senior year by filling up the stat sheet, scoring a school-record 43 points and finishing with 10 steals, nine rebounds, seven assists and four blocks to lead St. Bonaventure to a 94-39 win over Verdugo Hills in a season opener. Cosio went 18 of 24 from the field, including 7 of 11 from the 3-point line while coming within one rebound and three assists from a rare quadruple-double. Alynah Leon had an impressive double-double with 24 points and 10 rebounds and added six assists and five steals and Sophia Fernandez had 11 points, eight rebounds and five assists for the Seraphs.

Emma Anter finished with 19 points and seven rebounds, Brinley Anderson had a double-double with 15 points and 10 rebounds, Maddie Moward scored 15 points, and Mya Rodriguez had six rebounds and six assists as Ventura opened its season with a 55-45 win over Oaks Christian in the Conejo Valley Tip-Off Classic. It was the 600th career victory for Ventura head coach Ann Larson, who now boasts a 600-174 overall record. For the Lions, Presley Kushner scored 20 points, Bonita Liu had 12 points and Le'lani Lacey added nine points.

Freshman Annabelle Chinsio hit seven 3-pointers and finished with 29 points in her high school debut and senior Emerson Martin scored 16 points to lead Camarillo to a 65-54, season-opening win over Village Christian in the Conejo Valley Tip-Off Classic.

Deanna Pham hit seven 3-points to finish with 21 points, Aryanna Lopez had four 3-pointers and finished with 16 points, and Raquel Daringer scored 11 points to lead Thousand Oaks to a 63-46, season-opening win over Trinity Classical Academy in the Conejo Valley Tip-Off Classic.

Olivia Elsokary had a double-double with 14 points and 13 steals while amassing six assists and three rebounds, Amaya White scored 14 points, Sophia Forutan had six points, and Sydney Katz grabbed 11 rebounds and added five points as Westlake opened its season with a 47-25 win over St. Genevieve in the Conejo Valley Tip-Off Classic.

Maya Cunningham scored 13 points, Gia Angell had 12 points, Destinee Herrera and Sara Mateos each had eight points, and Sofia Gonzalez added seven points as Oxnard started its season with a 56-44 win over Righetti in the Conejo Valley Tip-Off Classic.

McKenna Daly scored 15 points and Morgan Love and Everley Prange each had eight points to lead Agoura to a 54-18 win over Torres in a season opener.

Simi Valley lost to Santa Barbara 48-25 in its season opener.

Jourdyn Lawrence scored six points for Foothill Tech in its 65-19 loss to Golden Valley in a season opener.

GALLERY: Moorpark boys basketball wins opener against Santa Clara

Logan Stotts poured in 26 points and added four rebounds and two steals, Tyson Howarth had 12 points, four rebounds and four assists, and Taylor McKee had nine points, three rebounds and three steals to lead Moorpark to a 62-43 win over Santa Clara in a season-opener. JJ Ward and DJ Hughes each scored 15 points for the Saints.

Sophomore Easton Holmes posted an impressive double-double by scoring 33 points and grabbing 15 rebounds, Jonathan Plax had a double-double with 22 points and 10 assists while adding four steals, Srikar Potluri had 13 points and four rebounds, and Ryan Niazi added 10 points and five rebounds to lead Oak Park to a 93-61, season-opening win over Culver City .

articles.title: Blue Jays Enter Race For Alex Vesia As Yankees Weigh Options
articles.summary: The Toronto Blue Jays are now pursuing Alex Vesia, creating a new hurdle for the Yankees. See the stats, the money, and what this means for the Bronx.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees have secured a reliable arm in Tim Hill with a one-year, $2.25 million deal that includes a 2028 club option, per Yanks Go Yard . Yet the search for top-tier left-handed relief continues as a division rival steps into the fray. The Toronto Blue Jays are now showing active interest in free agent Alex Vesia.

Vesia's tenure with the Dodgers yielded a 2.66 ERA and 6.3 bWAR between 2021 and 2026, reflecting a strong track record. The 30-year-old pitcher has logged 31 added postseason appearances since 2021, proving he can handle high-pressure moments, per The Good Phight .

The Blue Jays' interest in Vesia was first reported by FanSided on Sunday evening. Toronto is looking to fix a pitching staff that suffered a multitude of injuries during the 2026 season. They are also tracking righty starter Dustin May alongside Vesia. This dual interest suggests the Blue Jays are aiming for a major overhaul of their rotation and relief corps.

For the Yankees, losing out on Vesia would leave a gap in their late-inning plans. The team recently extended a $23.15 million qualifying offer to closer David Bednar. The deadline to accept or reject that one-year deal falls on Tuesday. If Bednar rejects the offer and signs elsewhere, the Yankees will need Vesia or a similar lefty to stabilize the seventh and eighth innings.

While Vesia remains a potent weapon, his recent performance shows some warning signs. While The Good Phight notes his strikeout rate fell slightly, the 31.2% K% remains deemed ridiculous by many observers. More concerning is that his walk rate spiked from 9.3% to 13.5%, per The Good Phight.

There is also a slight dip in pure stuff. Alex Vesia's fastball velocity dropped half a tick even though he is only 30, per The Good Phight. This small drop might indicate the pitcher is losing a bit of his edge or adjusting his mechanics. The Yankees must decide if his past success outweighs these recent trends in a crowded free-agent market.

The Yankees have already acted on one front by re-signing Hill, but the hunt for a second lefty is far from over. The presence of Toronto changes the dynamic, as the Blue Jays have the money and the need to make a splash. The clock is ticking on Bednar's decision, and the market for left-handed relievers is thin.

If the Blue Jays make a strong offer, the Yankees may have to look elsewhere or pay a premium to secure their target.

articles.title: Erling Haaland’s last-minute penalty sends Norway into Nations League quarter-finals
articles.summary: Haaland scored with the last kick of the game to send Norway into the quarter-finals, where they will play England, France or Germany
articles.body:
Erling Haaland scored a 96th-minute penalty with the last kick of the game to send Norway into the quarter-finals of the Nations League with victory over Denmark in Copenhagen.

Norway knew then needed to beat Denmark to leapfrog their opponents into second place in Group A4, with Portugal ensuring top spot by beating Wales in Cardiff.

They made a horror start, though, as the visitors found themselves 2-0 down inside 15 minutes as Rasmus Hojlund and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg put Denmark in control.

Norway started their comeback when Mads Hermansen lost possession under pressure from Martin Odegaard and Haaland tapped into the empty net before half-time.

Captain Odegaard equalised in the 83rd minute to give Norway further hope, before they won a last-gasp penalty as Joachim Andersen was penalised for handball in the box.

Haaland stepped up and kept his cool in front of the home fans in the Parken Stadium, taking off his shirt as Norway wildly celebrated their dramatic victory.

The World Cup quarter-finalists will now advance to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, where they could face either England, France or Germany in the last eight.

Denmark, who had thrashed group winners Portugal 4-1 away from home on Saturday, will instead go into a relegation play-off in March as they bid to keep their top-flight status.

articles.title: WWE Hall of Famer 'Cowboy' Bill Watts Dies at Age 87
articles.summary: WWE chief content officer Triple H announced Tuesday that Hall of Famer Bill Watts died at the age of 87.
articles.body:
WWE chief content officer Triple H announced Tuesday that Hall of Famer Bill Watts died at the age of 87.

"Just learned of the passing of "Cowboy" Bill Watts," he wrote on social media. "Bill performed across the United States and Japan, but is remembered for his contributions behind the scenes in various NWA promotions and eventually WCW. His Mid-South Wrestling featured future WWE Hall of Famers every week, each character having a distinct voice and style... and for those contributions, he was made a member of the WWE Hall of Fame class of 2009. We send our condolences to his loved ones."

Predicting Final Members of Team USA and Team Mexico 🔮

Watts played college football at Oklahoma and had a brief professional career in football before turning to professional wrestling. His most famous feud came with Bruno Sammartino, the WWWF champion at the time.

By the 1980s, Watts had transitioned into a role as a wrestling promoter, starting the Mid-South Wrestling (later the Universal Wrestling Federation). After selling that promotion he became the executive vice president of World Championship Wrestling, though his tenure was short.

He then briefly served as a booker for the WWF.

articles.summary: Arch Manning led a game-winning drive past the Tigers as Texas jumped to No. 5 in the College Football Playoff rankings, with Georgia holding at No. 1.
articles.body: The College Football Playoff committee has released its third iteration of rankings, and unlike the previous two, there isn’t much movement going on near the top. Curt Cignetti and the reigning national-champion Indiana Hoosiers may have wanted some teams above them at No. 9 to lose, but all eight managed a victory. So, how would the CFP committee view those wins in terms of movement? However, we have a new team at No. 5, with Arch Manning and Texas swapping places with Notre Dame from last week’s rankings, and it has everything to do with yet another ranked-opponent victory. It was cinema in Death Valley, as Manning led a game-winning touchdown drive to beat the Tigers, 22-21, and the CFP committee rewarded them for it. Texas has five wins in the top 25, the most of any team in the field, and it’s been clear this committee favors who you’ve beaten rather than who you’ve lost to. Just look at Arizona, who took the undefeated Utes down to the wire, but came away with its third loss of the year. But they went from No. 23 in last week’s rankings to No. 19, which is a CFP record in terms of spots moved after a loss. With Notre Dame and Miami at No. 6 and 7 respectively, we saw Indiana, coming off a statement win over a ranked USC Trojans squad, move into the No. 8 slot. Tennessee feel one spot to No. 9, while BYU rounded out the top 10. "What we were really impressed with as a committee was what Indiana did as an offense," CFP committee chair Hunter Yurachek told ESPN’s Rece Davis. " … That’s the thing that had been missing from Indiana this year." Finally, Wake Forest would be the last team in today at No. 11 with a 9-1 record, while Texas Tech would be the first team out at No. 12 due to the Group of 6 team, Boise State, who came in at No. 17 after jumping seven spots this week, needing a spot in the bracket. But it’s interesting to see two three-loss teams from the Big Ten, Oregon at No. 13 and Ohio State at No. 14, on the bubble and very much in the mix over the next couple of weeks.
